papers.title: The Fourier restriction problem for biradial functions
papers.abstract: We determine the exact strong-type Fourier restriction range for the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ on the class of $O(d-k)\times O(k)$-invariant functions, for every $d\geq4$ and $2\leq k\leq d-2$. This includes the critical estimates beyond the biradial Stein--Tomas endpoint left open by Mandel and Oliveira e Silva. The proof combines a weighted $L^2$ estimate for extension from a circular arc with the full two-dimensional restriction theorem. An appendix gives a direct proof of the classically conjectured range for axially symmetric functions on the whole sphere.

papers.title: The Inverse Problem of Velocity Reconstruction from Flow-Induced Magnetic Fields: Stability and Uniqueness
papers.abstract: The reconstruction of velocity fields from flow-induced magnetic measurements is a fundamental inverse problem in magnetohydrodynamics, with broad applications in geophysics, astrophysics, and metallurgy. To address the nonlinearity of the governing equations, the magnetic induction equation is linearized around a known, space-dependent background magnetic field. This reveals a coupled parabolic--hyperbolic system in which magnetic diffusion interacts with velocity advection along the background field lines. By decoupling these mechanisms into a two-stage framework, sufficient conditions are established for both the uniqueness and stability of the velocity recovery. The main result proves that the non-uniqueness arising from unobservable velocity perturbations parallel to the background field is eliminated when the velocity trace on the inflow boundary is prescribed alongside magnetic observations. The analysis yields global uniqueness and a quantitative stability estimate of hybrid type: a Lipschitz contribution from the inflow trace combined with a weaker modulus from the parabolic observation, reflecting the mixed parabolic--hyperbolic structure of the problem. These theoretical findings are validated through three-dimensional numerical simulations that demonstrate the robustness of the decoupled reconstruction approach under noisy conditions.

papers.title: Detecting Errors in Large Language Model Responses: The Incremental Predictive Value of Hidden States
papers.abstract: Although large language models support a wide range of tasks, hallucinations remain a major obstacle to user trust. When a model generates an answer, both its internal processing and final output vary with the question. Internal states are often expected to offer richer signals for hallucination detection. However, studies using these states typically report their standalone discrimination performance, while output-side comparisons often use simple baselines with weaker modeling capacity. We integrate output-side information available at inference time into a combined baseline and compare detection performance before and after adding hidden states under identical data splits and evaluation rules. Experiments cover open-ended generation and constrained multiple-choice tasks across different models. Adding hidden states improves AUROC by approximately 0.004 and 0.039 on the two tasks, respectively. Hidden states thus provide additional predictive information, but strong standalone detection performance can still yield only limited additional gains.

authors.name: Xiaofei Wang
authors.institution: Franche-Comté Électronique Mécanique Thermique et Optique - Sciences et Technologies

papers.title: Towards Interaction State Recognition in Sensorized Gecko-Inspired Adhesive Interfaces for Orbital Servicing
papers.abstract: Reliable contact establishment remains a critical challenge for autonomous on-orbit servicing (OOS), particularly when interacting with non-cooperative targets. Gecko-inspired dry adhesives provide a lightweight, passive, and residue-free solution for robotic capture in space, yet current systems operate in open loop, without the ability to estimate their own contact or adhesion state during interaction. This paper presents a real-time interaction-awareness framework that enables sensorized gecko-inspired adhesive interfaces to estimate their contact state throughout the adhesion lifecycle using embedded capacitive sensing. Five discrete interaction states (idle, proximity, contact, engaged, and disengaged) are classified using experimentally collected and augmented sensor data, enabling a comparative evaluation of six lightweight machine learning models suitable for embedded deployment. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest achieved the highest offline classification accuracy of 95.65%. For online deployment, combining Random Forest with a rule-based state machine improved accuracy from 78.02% to 93.14%, achieving a macro F1-score of 0.9343 while maintaining a 53 ms inference cycle. These results demonstrate that incorporating physics-consistent state constraints significantly improves robustness during realtime inference, representing a step toward interaction-aware capture in future autonomous orbital servicing missions.

papers.title: An Aldous-type tightness characterisation for the $M_1$ topology: replacing global modulus control by local control at stopping times
papers.abstract: Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

authors.name: Fabrice Wunderlich
authors.institution: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.title: MARE: An Open-Source Lunar Rover Simulator with Shadow Ground Truth for Perception and Autonomy
papers.abstract: Lunar surface exploration increasingly relies on autonomous rovers that must perceive and traverse unstructured terrain under extreme illumination conditions. Near the lunar poles, low sun elevations produce long, high-contrast shadows that challenge stereo vision, terrain segmentation, and localization. Developing perception and navigation algorithms for these conditions requires large amounts of sensor data with accurate ground truth, which field campaigns and analog facilities can only provide at high cost and with limited variety. This paper presents MARE (Modular Autonomy and Rendering Environment), an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2. MARE consists of three integrated components. Terrain Studio generates cratered and rocky lunar Digital Elevation Maps (DEMs) to build simulation scenes. A dedicated Unreal Engine project hosts two physics-based rovers with plugins for stereo, lidar, event, and Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) cameras, streaming time-stamped sensor data and pixel-accurate ground truth. Lastly, a Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) stack provides web-based mission control. Validation shows a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.79 between predicted and rendered shadows at low sun elevations, and stereo depth analysis verifies decreased pixel coverage in shadowed regions relative to sunlit terrain.

papers.title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
papers.abstract: Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie Rényi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation. This, in particular, settles the sample complexity of integer-order Rényi entropy estimation up to absolute constants in all regimes, closing the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds. Our concentration bound rests on a sensitivity analysis of collision count, and the matching lower bound on a sharp analysis of detecting a hidden spike in a plateau distribution.

papers.title: Globular Clusters GMRT Pulsar Survey (GCGPS) III: ORION - a multi-beam acceleration search pipeline
papers.abstract: Globular clusters host rich millisecond pulsar populations, but the known population remains incomplete. We present the observing strategy for Phase II of the Globular Clusters GMRT Pulsar Survey (GCGPS), which uses the SPOTLIGHT system to form 160 synthesised beams simultaneously, substantially expanding the instantaneous field of view compared with the two phased-array beams of Phase I. The configuration is tunable through the beam overlap and the number of contributing antennas, allowing spatial coverage to be balanced against sensitivity. We quantify the sensitivity losses from intra-channel dispersion smearing and finite sampling, which motivate the adopted dispersion-measure limits of 50 and 150 pc/cc for Bands 3 and 4. To process the resulting data, we introduce ORION, a GPU-accelerated pipeline that combines the high-throughput Fourier-domain filtering of PULSCAN with localised parameter refinement using PRESTO. In single-beam tests with simulated binary pulsars, ORION reduces processing time by a factor of approximately 15 to 30 relative to the CPU-based Phase I pipeline, with comparable or higher folded detection significance. On-sky validation with Cycle 49 observations recovered four known globular cluster pulsars with spin periods of approximately 5.4 to 406 ms. Using eight GPUs and 64 CPU cores, ORION processes full 160-beam observations in approximately 0.25 to 0.33 times the observation duration, corresponding to three to four times real-time throughput. Together, the Phase II strategy and ORION provide a scalable framework for expanding globular cluster pulsar searches, with future development targeting highly accelerated and jerked binary systems.

authors.name: Paulo C. C. Freire
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

authors.name: Junhao Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution
papers.abstract: Adapting a forecasting system to a changing world classically means retraining. We ask whether the task of continually learning regimes for time series forecasting can be represented by a piece of text: a guidance block, evolved by outcome-driven reflection and used in a frozen LLM forecaster's prompt. On a refreshed multimodal benchmark (weekly search indices, daily currencies, daily commodities, each window paired with web-retrieved news), we run GEPA-style prompt evolution under strict contamination control to prevent the data leakage common in timeseries benchmarks: the forecaster's knowledge cutoff predates every evaluated window. A 900-word evolved guidance carried by Llama-3.3-70B beats TimeSeries Foundation Models (TSFMs) on held-out data (GM MASE 0.776 vs. 0.898 for TabPFN-TS-3), transfers to more recent models without measurable loss, and costs dollars rather than GPU-days to update. We characterize the loop: out-of-loop gains concentrate in the first reflection, in-loop improvements overstate out-of-loop gains 2-3x unless an untouched monitor arbitrates, and error-only objectives silently suppress the text modality. We provide two extensions. First, compiling the guidance into executable code with a TSFM as a callable tool recovers most of the gain deterministically. Second, ablations show the advantage widens at short horizons and that removing the news text does not hurt the guided forecaster, consistent with the text's value being distilled into policy during learning. We argue that continual prompt evolution is a practical, training-free alternative to retraining for multimodal forecasting.

papers.title: Influence of Ideal, Cubic, and Multiparameter Helmholtz Equations of State on the Static and Dynamic Performance of Porous Aerostatic Journal Bearings
papers.abstract: Porous aerostatic gas bearings are commonly modeled using the ideal-gas law, although non-ideal thermodynamic behavior may become relevant for alternative working fluids. This study quantifies the influence of the thermodynamic closure on the stationary and dynamic response of porous aerostatic journal bearings. A finite-volume formulation couples the compressible Reynolds equation with three-dimensional Darcy flow, retaining transient gas storage in both domains. Density is used as the primary thermodynamic variable, allowing the ideal-gas, van der Waals, Soave--Redlich--Kwong, Peng--Robinson, and multiparameter Helmholtz equations of state to be evaluated within an otherwise unchanged bearing model. Air, R1234yf, and R1234ze(E) are considered. For air, EOS-induced differences remain negligible over the investigated range. For the refrigerants, the ideal-gas approximation produces several-percent deviations, with supplied mass flow and dynamic force response being particularly sensitive. The cubic equations substantially reduce these deviations, with the employed Peng--Robinson formulation providing the closest agreement with the Helmholtz reference for both refrigerants at a computational cost comparable to the other cubic models. The results identify density and differential compressibility as the main thermodynamic quantities governing the propagation of EOS errors into mass transport and transient gas storage.

papers.title: Real-Time Disturbance-Aware Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors in Spatially Varying Winds
papers.abstract: Reliable quadrotor flight in disturbed environments requires predictive models that remain accurate as unmodeled aerodynamic effects change during deployment. We introduce a disturbance-aware Koopman Control Family (DA-KCF) framework that preserves an offline-identified nominal model while learning only a disturbance-induced correction online. A reference-dependent KCF is first learned from simulation data and calibrated using limited hardware data. During deployment, the nominal KCF remains fixed while a lightweight residual ensemble learns a low-dimensional disturbance correction from causal state-command-state transitions. The Adaptive DA-KCF model is incorporated into MPC, where disturbance corrections are evaluated along the prediction horizon to optimize position and yaw references sent to the onboard stabilizing controller. Hardware experiments on a nano-quadrotor under uniform wind and a spatially varying wake demonstrate that online adaptation improves multi-step prediction and trajectory tracking as disturbance-induced model mismatch increases, while satisfying real-time control requirements.

papers.title: Design and implementation of thermal control strategy for micro-size lunar exploration rover hakuto
papers.abstract: The research focuses on the thermal interface design of the HAKUTO Rover Flight Model (FM) and its evaluation using the final thermal vacuum experiment. Initially, an analytical thermal model was developed, dividing the rover into six distinct radiating surfaces. The surface temperature of the rover was then determined based on its orientation relative to the solar radiative flux, as well as other thermal factors such as lunar radiation, solar albedo, and conduction from the lunar regolith. By considering the impact of these heat sources, suitable mounting locations for the avionics and the angle of the solar panels were determined to optimize the rover's thermal performance and power generation while ensuring the rover's mass remained under 4 kg. After the preliminary thermal analysis, numerical computational simulations were conducted to further elaborate on the thermal response of the final HAKUTO Rover FM design, which was then verified through a thermal balance test in a vacuum environment.

authors.name: John Walker
authors.institution: Istituto Scientifico Romagnolo per lo Studio e la Cura dei Tumori

papers.title: Uncountably many settled elements are never Frobenius elements
papers.abstract: Boston and Jones conjectured that given a number field $K$, a quadratic polynomial $f\in K[x]$, and an element $α\in K$ such that the arboreal Galois representation $ρ_{f,α}:\text{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$ attached to the pair $(f,α)$ is well defined, any element in the image of such representation that is a Frobenius for an unramified prime of $K$ is a settled element. We exhibit an explicit uncountable subset $S\subseteq \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$, consisting of pairwise non-conjugate settled elements, such that no matter how $K,f,α$ are chosen, no element of $S$ can be a Frobenius for any ramified or unramified prime of $K$.

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Model for the Evolution of a Social Network
papers.abstract: Echo chambers and filter bubbles provide a framework to view communication and connection in a social network age. Such systems are characterised by isolated communities regurgitating information which reinforces prior beliefs. Theoretical analysis of echo chambers is suited for a network science approach to understand the mechanics of information influences between users. Here, we propose an evolutionary network model that extends the Quoter Model, rewiring edges according to cross-entropy between text-generating nodes. Parameters characterise binary reinforcement vs exploration node intents, determining whether a node will seek high or low novelty neighbours, measured by cross-entropy. Through an empirical simulation study, we observe emergent model attributes. Specifically, we compare to a Watts--Strogatz model, highlighting parameter regions of high clustering and hyper-exploration. Further, we identify a quality of disjoint communities akin to rudimentary echo chamber structures. These findings underscore user behaviours that drive echo chamber entrenchment, contextualising future social network analysis.

papers.title: Multi-agent LLMs on the Cloud-Edge-IoT Continuum: A Systematic Mapping Study on Architectures, Deployment, and Evaluation
papers.abstract: LLM applications are increasingly built as systems of cooperating components rather than as single prompt-response pipelines. IoT applications add constraints of their own, because sensing, reasoning, control, and actuation are spread across devices, edge nodes, and cloud services to meet latency, privacy, and bandwidth requirements. How multi-agent LLM systems are organized and deployed across this cloud-edge-IoT continuum has not been mapped systematically. We therefore conducted a systematic mapping study. From 831 records retrieved up to March 2026, we selected 45 primary studies and classified each one by architecture family, deployment pattern, application domain, and evaluation practice. We also recorded how each system was evaluated and whether its code or data are public. Five architecture families recur in the corpus. Specialized agent teams run next to sensors, planners delegate subtasks to workers, and small local models cooperate with large cloud models. A fourth group federates model adaptation across devices, and a large fifth group builds the supporting infrastructure for offloading, communication, memory, and serving. Deployment relies on six recurring patterns, ranging from local-only execution to control loops gated by policy checks or human approval. Twenty-four of the 45 studies target IoT, industrial, smart-home, healthcare, vehicular, or robotics settings, and 29 evaluate on physical hardware, where open models below 8B parameters dominate. Based on the mapping, we list the reporting items needed to make future evaluations comparable, give deployment guidance for common IoT constraints, and identify open problems.

papers.title: From Comparison to Selection: Enhancing Cross-Scale Generalization of Pointer Networks Trained with Reinforcement Learning for Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
papers.abstract: Vehicle routing in delivery and logistics remains challenging as the number of clients varies. Classical approaches based on mixed-integer programming and heuristics can scale poorly or require problem-specific design, motivating learning-based alternatives. Reinforcement learning is particularly promising, provided a single policy can generalise across problem sizes without retraining. Although attention-based Pointer Networks are inherently size-agnostic, their solution quality degrades under both upscaling and downscaling. Using the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) as a controlled proxy, we investigate this degradation and identify three contributing factors: shifts in node density, attention dispersion, and dilution of the mean-pooled graph context. We systematically compare architecture-wide, encoder-side, and decoder-side modifications to address these limitations and propose a learned, permutation-invariant graph-context aggregation mechanism, implemented as a weighted average and as Set2Set. Results reveal distinct requirements for transfer in each direction: entropy-based attention scaling reduces the CVRP20-to-CVRP100 performance gap by 1.41 percentage points, while the proposed aggregation methods achieve the largest improvement on the more challenging CVRP100-to-CVRP20 transfer, approximately 0.9 percentage points. Exploiting this complementarity, we introduce an approach selector that chooses the best model for each training-target size pair. The selector reduces cost relative to the reference model across all nine seen train-test pairs and eight of nine pairs involving unseen sizes (CVRP35, CVRP75, and CVRP200), achieving improvements of up to 3.2%.

papers.title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
papers.abstract: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Treviño's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

authors.name: Larry Rolen
authors.institution: TH Köln - University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.

papers.title: LocoPilot: Single-Operator Bilateral Teleoperation for Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Learning loco-manipulation policies requires demonstrations that capture coordinated base and arm motion on the target embodiment. Robot-free interfaces allow demonstrations to be collected independently of the target robot, increasing flexibility but without directly capturing platform-specific commands, proprioception, and body-mounted observations. On-robot teleoperation allows to capture these signals directly, but requires an interface capable of commanding the complete system concurrently. This paper presents LocoPilot, a single-operator bilateral teleoperation and data-collection framework implemented on a 12-DoF Unitree Go2 quadruped equipped with a 6-DoF AgileX Piper L manipulator, an Intel RealSense D435 wrist camera, and an Intel RealSense D405 head camera. A second 6-DoF Piper L arm, used as the leader and two handheld controllers provide simultaneous control of the base, body posture, manipulator, and gripper. The follower arm interaction forces are estimated without a dedicated force/torque sensor and rendered to the operator through a passivity-constrained haptic channel. A ROS~2 pipeline records synchronized multimodal observations together with a unified 11D action shared by teleoperation and policy deployment. Compared to prior work, LocoPilot uniquely unifies robot-in-the-loop legged data collection, force feedback without motion-capture instrumentation, and the same action interface at deployment. We evaluate the interface across multiple loco-manipulation tasks and validate the complete collection-to-deployment pipeline by fine-tuning MolmoAct2 \cite{MOLMO} on pick-and-place demonstrations and deploying on the physical robot without action retargeting or additional inverse kinematics. Code available at: https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/LocoPilot

papers.title: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not
papers.abstract: How can we effectively oversee AI systems that surpass human intelligence? AI Safety via Debate proposes that two AI systems argue opposing positions and a judge, either a human or a weaker model, decides which is correct. By facilitating supervisors in providing high-quality training signals, debate aims to encourage truthful and safe behavior from AI systems whose capabilities exceed our own. However, human judgment is not neutral: people often rely on biases which advanced AI systems may learn to exploit. Drawing on insights from collective intelligence and social cognition, this paper investigates whether debate can guide human and LLM supervisors toward the truth despite their prior beliefs. We evaluate several protocol configurations. We also explore setups inspired by the wisdom of the crowd such as the number and diversity of judges, as well as interaction mechanisms including deliberation and voting. Overall, we find that debate increases accuracy relative to prior beliefs for human judges, whereas the consultancy baseline, in which a single expert argues for one answer, does not. For weaker language models, however, the results are mixed: debate provides no comparable gains in most settings and can even reduce accuracy. Among multi-judge protocols, weighted voting produces the highest accuracy for human supervisors, whereas for LLMs none of them significantly improves group accuracy, even as the number of judges increases. Notably, the behavior of minority judges in non-diverse deliberation protocols suggests that, under symmetric settings, incorrect positions could be more persuasive than correct ones. These findings support debate as a viable path toward scalable human oversight, but cast doubt on its benefits for weaker AI supervisors, raising concerns about fully automated training and control pipelines in high-stakes settings.

authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: ASTROLABE: A 3D Particle-Level Surrogate for Cosmology Simulation with Physical Flow Matching
papers.abstract: The microphysics of dark matter (DM) is imprinted on cosmological structure across an enormous dynamic range. Nonlinear cosmological observables are most reliably modeled with N-body and hydrodynamic simulations. However, systematic N-body scans over DM theory space are prohibitively expensive. Machine learning emulators provide a possible solution, but are currently limited by either low resolution or only the ability to emulate specific observables. We introduce Astrolabe, a flow-matching-based generative emulator designed to be free of both constraints. Astrolabe acts directly on the 6N phase-space coordinates of N individual particles. With no voxel grid in the output, there is no voxel-resolution ceiling, and in principle any observable can be measured from inference. Astrolabe is computationally tractable via a field-particle hybrid transformer in which every particle cross-attends to multiscale field tokens, so compute and memory are linear in N. Astrolabe incorporates physical flow matching by taking the prior distribution for the flow to be approximate COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (COLA)-based coordinates rather than unphysical noise, with momentum and mass conservation enforced at all points along flow time. In the Lambda-CDM cases we test, Astrolabe produces realistic fields with accurate power spectra, halo mass functions, velocity profiles, and halo density profiles. We also observe out-of-distribution generalization, with accurate emulation of dark-acoustic oscillation initial conditions. Astrolabe is also capable of being fine-tuned to simulate very large N and we demonstrate this by emulating a TNG50-3-dark simulation at a fraction of the cost. This method represents a first step toward a general and powerful cosmology simulation surrogate, which may eventually permit the inclusion of baryonic physics and a systematic exploration of richer dark sector interactions.

papers.title: LEAF: LUT-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs
papers.abstract: We introduce Lookup-table (LUT)-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs (LEAF). LEAF is the first nanosecond-scale LUT-aware transformer for FPGAs. Deploying transformers that are large enough to perform well, small enough to fit on an FPGA, and fast enough to meet the sub-microsecond timescales required by real-time systems such as those at CERN remains difficult, since the same attention mechanism that gives these models their high expressivity also makes them costly to implement in hardware. LEAF converts the query, key, and value projections and the final output feed-forward layer into FPGA-native layers with LUT-aware training, creating the first LUT-aware transformer and linformer layers built for ultra-low-latency inference. Attention resists LUT-aware training because it multiplies two activations where the method needs a constant weight to tabulate; LEAF tabulates the attention block's constant matrix-vector multiplications and leaves the rest in arithmetic form. On a standard jet tagging benchmark this improves accuracy by 1.8 percentage points while using 2.9 times fewer LUTs than the previous state-of-the-art sub-microsecond transformer at the same input size. Our most efficient LEAF-based linformer with 64 input particles reaches 80.4% classification accuracy at 28k LUTs and 35ns.

papers.title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
papers.abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

papers.title: Sound Matching with a Differentiable Karplus-Strong Algorithm
papers.abstract: We present a self-supervised, event-based sound matching model using a differentiable extended Karplus-Strong algorithm. To avoid relying on external onset and fundamental frequency detectors, we explore training methodologies combining parameter losses on synthetic data with audio losses. We demonstrate that time-domain fractional delay interpolation provides gradient accuracy comparable to frequency-sampling while avoiding time-aliasing in highly resonant time-varying scenarios. Through systematic gradient analysis, we reveal that standard spectral losses provide no meaningful directional gradients for onset times, heavily degrading joint training. Training exclusively with parameter losses on synthetic data effectively learns fundamental frequency, timbral parameters, and onset times, but struggles to generalise to monophonic studio recordings of plucked guitar. External detectors combined with audio losses generalise best, isolating the model to timbre optimisation. While our Karplus-Strong decoder recovers interpretable parameters and naturally captures the transient characteristics of plucked guitar, Harmonics plus Noise baselines yield higher reconstruction fidelity by most metrics.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Plate Parameter Estimation with Differentiable and Particle-Swarm Refinement
papers.abstract: We present two Transformer-based methods for Task A of the 1st DAFx Parameter Estimation Challenge, which requires estimating six effective physical parameters of a synthetic plate-reverb model from its impulse response (IR). Method A1 combines an Audio Spectrogram Transformer encoder and Transformer regressor with differentiable IR refinement. Method A2 uses the same encoder to condition a continuous normalizing flow and refines sampled candidates using particle swarm optimisation (PSO) and gradient polishing. Both methods preserve the absolute IR scale to recover surface density. On a synthetic holdout set of 100 IRs, both refinement procedures reduce waveform and parameter errors by more than three orders of magnitude relative to the unrefined neural outputs. The PSO-based pipeline achieves the lowest errors, indicating near-perfect recovery in this matched synthetic setting.

papers.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis
papers.abstract: Oddly Satisfying Videos (OSVs) can evoke strong viewer responses through repetitive motion, visual tactility, and ASMR-like sounds despite containing few explicit semantic emotion cues. This makes OSVs a challenging setting for Video Emotion Analysis (VEA), since most existing methods focus on semantic video content and under-model the physical sensory dynamics that shape viewer responses. To support Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis (OSVEA), we construct the Oddly Satisfying Video Dataset (OSVD), comprising 12,000 annotated 5-second clips. Each clip provides viewer-emotion labels under video-only, audio-only, and audio-visual conditions, together with explanations grounded in visual and acoustic sensory evidence. Building on OSVD, we propose PI-MLLM, a psychophysics-inspired multimodal large language model that integrates Modality-Specific Dynamics Alignment (MSDA) and Coalition-Based Audio-Visual Attribution (CAVA). MSDA uses auxiliary prediction objectives to align modality representations with visual motion and acoustic energy-onset dynamics. CAVA evaluates emotion scores across modality coalitions and applies Shapley attribution to identify the dominant modality and determine whether visual and auditory evidence is synergistic or conflicting. Experiments show that PI-MLLM improves both viewer-side emotion prediction and sensory-grounded explanation quality, suggesting the value of physical sensory cues to video emotion analysis.

authors.name: Shiguang Shan
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Space-time large deviations for continuum birth-and-death processes
papers.abstract: We establish a space-time large deviation principle for the empirical process of spatial birth-and-death dynamics in the continuum with area interaction at arbitrary inverse temperature, including the free evolution. The good rate function is the dynamical specific relative entropy with respect to the dynamics, and the result holds on the space of space-time stationary laws on the Skorokhod path space, equipped with the topology of weak convergence. For the time marginals of the empirical process, we identify the rate function in terms of the Hellinger distance between the birth and the death measure of the observed point process, which vanishes exactly at the translation-invariant Gibbs point processes. This proves a continuum version of conjectures of Dai Pra and Handa, and connects space-time large deviations with entropy production.

papers.title: BIBO stability in infinite dimensions: extensions and limitations of finite-dimensional theory
papers.abstract: The study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of infinite-dimensional systems gives rise to difficulties that do not occur in the classical finite-dimensional setting. In this paper, we resolve several questions concerning the definition and characterisation of BIBO stability in the framework of system nodes. In particular, we show that $\mathrm C^\infty$-BIBO stability need not imply $L^\infty$-BIBO stability in general, but that the two notions are equivalent when the output space is reflexive. Furthermore, we investigate to what extent classical results extend to the infinite-dimensional setting, including the relation between BIBO stability and exponential stability under controllability and observability assumptions.

papers.title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
papers.abstract: As computer-use agents (CUAs) move to long-horizon workflows spanning multiple applications, undetected errors can silently corrupt persistent state and cause cascading failures in subsequent actions. Reliable error detection and recovery have become critical bottlenecks for building robust CUAs. However, existing benchmarks focus primarily on end-to-end task performance, providing limited insight into whether agents can detect and recover from errors during execution. The few benchmarks that evaluate recovery rely largely on manually injected errors, which may not reflect the types or horizons of failures induced by real agent policies. We introduce CUA-Recovery, a benchmark comprising test and training suites across multiple desktop applications. We construct it using ReRail, a framework for synthesizing long-horizon tasks and trajectories in a persistent desktop environment. ReRail composes MyPCBench tasks into new long-horizon workflows with executable ground truth, collects verifier-confirmed failures from multiple policies, and turns them into verified recovery trajectories. CUA-Recovery comprises a human-verified test suite of 2,250 erroneous states over 100 tasks and a training suite of 8.6K trajectories over 377 tasks. Evaluation on the test suite shows that agents struggle both to recognize inherited errors and to complete the task. Across six agents and six takeover depths, Error Awareness Rate (EAR) reaches at most 44.0% and Pass@3 at most 25.5%. After fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on the training suite, its average EAR rises from 19.9% to 35.2% on held-out recovery states, and its Rubric Score goes from 5.0% to 16.1%. It also gains 15.3 points on MyPCBench and 10.8 points on Odysseys for Pass@3, showing that the training trajectories help both with recovery and with completing tasks from a clean start. Our code is available at https://github.com/xu-hu-2002/CUA-Recovery.

papers.title: Runtime Semantic Discovery for Evolving Action Alphabets
papers.abstract: Runtime Verification typically assumes a fixed alphabet of observable actions. This assumption becomes fragile in evolving software systems, where updates, reconfigurations, or architectural changes may rename, split, or fuse actions while preserving the system's high-level intent. In these cases, previously valid monitors and specifications may become misaligned with the running system. In this paper, we study runtime semantic discovery, namely the problem of identifying whether newly observed actions play the same operational role as previously known ones, without reconstructing a global behavioral model. To this end, we propose a local and runtime-computable notion of action similarity based on the neighbor contexts in which actions occur within execution traces. We define a family of k-neighbor equivalences and use them to compare systems whose observable alphabets differ. Our approach is intentionally lightweight: it does not aim to fully characterize behavioral preservation, but rather to identify candidate semantic correspondences between actions in evolving systems. We discuss the expressive power and limitations of neighbor-based equivalence and show how inferred correspondences can support the adaptation of runtime monitors and specifications under selected classes of alphabet evolution.

papers.title: The GenAI Who Knew Too Little: Revisiting Transactive Memory Systems in Human GenAI Collaboration
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming knowledge work, creating new collaborative dynamics that challenge tradi-tional human-human interaction patterns. This study investigates how Transactive Memory Systems (TMS) manifest in human-GenAI collabora-tion. Through qualitative interpretive interviews with 14 knowledge work-ers and thematic analysis, we identified distinct TMS manifestations across its three main dimensions: (1) regarding specialization, expertise recogni-tion exhibited asymmetry. Humans developed awareness of GenAI capabili-ties while GenAI demonstrated only temporary recognition of human exper-tise; (2) in terms of credibility, humans formed ambivalent trust relation-ships with GenAI, simultaneously attributing expertise to the latter while implementing additional verification processes; and (3) concerning coor-dination, where humans primarily directed more passive GenAI systems lacking initiative, resulting in hierarchical interaction patterns and unidi-rectional information flow. Our findings reveal that TMS manifests differ-ently in human-GenAI compared to human-human collaboration, necessitat-ing theoretical adaptations including trust markers, acknowledging GenAI's absent metamemory, and identifying its temporary memory.

papers.title: A Pair-Weighted Reciprocal-Cost Representation of the von Weizsäcker Functional
papers.abstract: We investigate pair-weighted lattice energies constructed from the reciprocal ratio cost $J(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+x^{-1})-1$ and their connection to the von Weizsäcker kinetic-energy functional. When the pair weight depends only on the common multiplicative amplitude scale and is quadratic under uniform amplitude rescaling, it takes the form $B(u,v)=Cuv$. For the normalization $C=1$, the weighted edge cost reduces exactly to $\frac{1}{2}(u-v)^2$ for arbitrary positive neighboring amplitudes, without requiring a small-deviation expansion. On a Cartesian lattice, the resulting discrete energy converges to $\frac{1}{2}\int |\nabla u|^2,d\mathbf r$, with leading correction $-\frac{h^2}{24}\sum_k\int(\partial_k^2u)^2,d\mathbf r+O(h^4)$ under the stated regularity conditions. Identifying $u=\sqrtρ$ and restoring the factor $\hbar^2/m$ yields the von Weizsäcker functional. By contrast, the unweighted ratio cost approaches a scale-invariant log-Dirichlet action and does not have kinetic-energy dimensions. Numerical benchmarks confirm the expected lattice convergence and assess the discretization error in smooth, nodal, cusp, and molecular cases. For $\mathrm{H}_2^+$ densities obtained from aug-cc-pV5Z orbitals, a four-grid least-squares $h^2+h^4$ extrapolation agrees with orbital kinetic energies within $1.5\times10^{-4}$ relative over $R=1$--$6,a_0$. Alternative extrapolations indicate a conservative sensitivity of up to approximately $5\times10^{-4}$. The construction therefore provides a conditional exact discrete representation of the von Weizsäcker sector rather than an approximation to the complete noninteracting kinetic functional.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
papers.abstract: Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/runtime-barrier-monitor.

papers.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as research collaborators for hypothesis refinement, methodological planning, and technical analysis across multi-turn interactions. In this setting, a useful assistant must be accurate, methodologically justified, logically consistent, and token-efficient. Current alignment approaches rarely achieve all of these together. Instruction-tuned models gain conversational quality through verbosity, and we show that science-agnostic general collaborative rewards compress responses at the expense of scientific rigor. We propose CollabSciReM, a goal-conditioned reward framework that decomposes the session-level reward into conversational quality, scientific rigor, and structural efficiency. We also introduce SciQuality, a pairwise evaluation of multi-turn research conversations grounded in 300 held-out scientific papers and scored on six dimensions: methodological soundness, justification, logical consistency, factual correctness, novelty, and responsiveness. Fine-tuned on 8.62K synthetic research conversations, CollabSciReM is preferred on SciQuality over a science-agnostic reward baseline trained on the same data for all four Llama and Qwen models, including a 65.3% win rate at matched response length. For the 7B and 8B models, CollabSciReM outperforms the science-agnostic reward baseline on the primary metric in 8 of 10 single- and multi-turn benchmark settings. In a blind study, domain experts rated CollabSciReM significantly higher on novelty than the general-reward variant and reported fewer hallucinated responses than both the general-reward variant and the base model.

papers.title: Physical AI for Intralogistics: Benchmarking the NVIDIA Sim-to-Real Ecosystem for Cosmos-Enhanced COMPASS Navigation on Industrial Mobile Robots
papers.abstract: Classical robot navigation stacks are reliable but often require re-engineering for each new robot type and site. Learning-based navigation shifts this effort from hand-tuned parameters to data generation and training, where a policy adapts to each new embodiment or facility by fine-tuning in simulation. Whether policies adapted this way stay reliable on real industrial robots has seen little systematic testing. We study this for NVIDIA's X-Mobility and COMPASS workflow for training learned navigation policies on Idealworks robots. In simulation, we extend the COMPASS benchmark with two embodiments, the differential-drive iw$\mkern-1.5mu.\mkern-1.5mu$hub and an omnidirectional Humanoid Mobile Platform (HMP), and with a digital twin of the Idealworks R&D center. For the real world, we fine-tune X-Mobility on data from this digital twin, with and without sim-to-real variants generated by NVIDIA Cosmos, train COMPASS on top of it from scratch in the digital twin, deploy the resulting policies on the iw$\mkern-1.5mu.\mkern-1.5mu$hub's onboard Jetson AGX Xavier, and benchmark them in the Idealworks R&D center against COMPASS trained only on NVIDIA's environments and the existing Idealworks navigation stack on task success, efficiency, safety, smoothness and onboard compute. Running every static scenario both in a digital-twin replica and in the real facility measures the sim-to-real gap and how far Cosmos-augmented data closes it. Training in the digital twin with Cosmos sim-to-real augmentation raises the real-world success rate of learned navigation from 65.3% to 91.7% across four scenarios and nearly halves its weighted travel time compared with simulation-only training, bringing it within 8.3 points of the production navigation stack, fully onboard; with an integrated global planner, it also reaches far, occluded goals in every trial.
papers.intro:
Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) have become a core component of modern intralogistics, moving material between storage, production and shipping areas without fixed infrastructure. Their navigation is typically built as a modular pipeline: the robot localizes itself in a prior map, a global planner computes a route to the goal, and a local planner follows that route while avoiding obstacles, as in the widely used ROS 2 navigation stack Nav2 (Macenski et al., 2020). The local planners of such stacks are hand-designed, for example the dynamic window approach (Fox et al., 1997) or timed elastic bands (Rösmann et al., 2017), and operate on costmaps built from lidar and depth sensors.

The local planners of such stacks are hand-designed, for example the dynamic window approach (Fox et al., 1997) or timed elastic bands (Rösmann et al., 2017), and operate on costmaps built from lidar and depth sensors.

These stacks are mature and dependable in the conditions they were engineered for, but they are expensive to extend. Their behavior emerges from many interacting parameters, such as cost weights, inflation radii, velocity and acceleration limits and recovery behaviors, which must be re-tuned for every new robot geometry, drive configuration and facility layout. Their perception is largely geometric: an obstacle is an occupied cell, with no notion of what it is or how it will move, which limits their behavior around people, other vehicles and semi-structured clutter. As fleets grow to more robot types and more sites, this per-robot and per-site engineering becomes a dominant cost of deployment.

As fleets grow to more robot types and more sites, this per-robot and per-site engineering becomes a dominant cost of deployment.

Physical AI, the application of learned models to systems that perceive and act in the physical world, offers a different path: rather than being engineered, a navigation policy is learned from data and improves as more data becomes available. Several developments now make this practical. GPU-accelerated simulation such as Isaac Lab (Mittal et al., 2023) trains policies across thousands of parallel environments, which makes interaction data cheap. World models learn compact, predictive representations of the environment from which behavior can be learned (Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018). Navigation foundation models trained on data from many robots, such as GNM, ViNT and NoMaD (Shah et al., 2023a; Shah et al., 2023b; Sridhar et al., 2024), show that a single policy can drive different embodiments, in line with the cross-embodiment results of large-scale robot learning (Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2024). Training in simulation, however, raises its own challenge: a policy that performs well in simulation can fail on a real robot, because rendered images, physics and sensor noise never match reality exactly. This sim-to-real gap is the main obstacle to deploying simulation-trained policies (Zhao et al., 2020). A classical answer is domain randomization, which varies textures, lighting and other simulation parameters during training so that the real world appears to the policy as just another variation (Tobin et al., 2017). Generative world foundation models such as NVIDIA Cosmos (NVIDIA, 2025a) take this a step further: they turn simulated footage into photorealistic variations that preserve its geometry and motion, bringing the training data closer to what a robot’s cameras see in a real facility.

Together, these advances make learned navigation policies the natural next step for industrial navigation. A learned policy adapts to a new robot or a new site through data and fine-tuning rather than manual re-engineering; it can use camera images and the semantics they carry, not only geometry; and a single training pipeline can serve a whole fleet of embodiments. Two questions stand between this promise and industrial deployment: whether learned policies remain reliable outside simulation, on real robots in real facilities, and whether they can match the production navigation stacks they would replace on the metrics that matter in operation, namely task success, efficiency, safety and onboard compute.

COMPASS freezes the X-Mobility policy and trains a residual policy on top of it with reinforcement learning in Isaac Lab, learning only the corrections a given embodiment needs, either as a specialist for one robot or as a generalist distilled across several.

papers.title: Discount Yourself: Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip for Decentralised Learning under Client Outages
papers.abstract: Decentralised federated learning (DFL) trains personalised models on devices that average with their neighbours rather than with a central server. Real devices, however, are often offline for hours or days, and a client returning from an outage can recover only by aggregating the models its neighbourhood holds. We observe that the stalest of these models is usually the client's own, a case that existing staleness-aware rules, which discount only the models a client receives, do not address. We formalise aggregation after an outage as estimating the state of a fully available network and derive three principles. First, the receiver must be discounted like any neighbour. Every rule that weights it at least as much as each neighbour has an error that grows without bound with the outage, whereas discounting all candidates by relative staleness keeps the error bounded. Second, staleness must be measured as inherited lag rather than age, since local training resets a model's age but not the lag it absorbed from stale neighbours. We introduce the effective lag, which tracks this quantity at the cost of one scalar per message. Third, the discount must be steep, because absorbed lag persists in every later round. These principles define Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip (SFG), a family of drop-in aggregation rules with the communication and computation of decentralised federated averaging, whose guarantees hold for the stale receiver itself. On three image benchmarks and eight outage processes, including real smartphone availability traces, the lag-based members SFG-L and SFG-Cut consistently outperform decentralised federated averaging and recent age-of-information rules, and ablations show that each principle is necessary. The analysis also explains why tuned limited merging from gossip learning is effective.

papers.title: Functions determining few direction: the final missing case
papers.abstract: By results of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme and Szőnyi, and of Ball, if a function $f: {\mathbb F}_q\to{\mathbb F}_q$ determines fewer than $(q+3)/2$ directions, then $f-f(0)$ is linear over a subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$, except possibly when $q$ is even and $f$ determines exactly $q/2+1$ directions. We settle this case: $f-f(0)$ is then additive. Hence every small minimal blocking set of Rédei type in PG(2,$q$) is linear.

papers.title: $\mathrm{v}$-numbers of powers of edge ideals of cubic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.

papers.title: From Proper Scoring Rules and Edge Biases to Mumford-Shah Models: Robust Unsupervised Hyperspectral Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral images provide a rich representation of the underlying spectrum for each pixel, allowing for a pixel-wise classification/segmentation into different classes. As the availability of labeled hyperspectral images is limited and the acquisition of labeled training data is time-consuming, unsupervised segmentation methods are important in hyperspectral image segmentation. Spectral variability, mixed pixels, noise as well as high correlation between neighboring spectral bands make this task challenging. We present a feature-agnostic, unsupervised hyperspectral segmentation framework based on the piecewise-constant Mumford-Shah functional. Our framework turns a strictly proper scoring rule and a family of parametric probability distributions into an indicator function for the Mumford-Shah functional, and we naturally generalize some previous Mumford-Shah based models for image segmentation this way. Our focus will be on heavy-tailed elliptical distributions, the negative log-likelihood score and the score based on the beta-divergence to deal with the heavy outliers in hyperspectral imaging. Using the interplay between the calculus of variations and statistics, we also propose a robustness step to estimate the statistical parameters of these heavy-tailed elliptical distributions. In addition, an edge bias, which contains prior boundary information, is incorporated into both the data fidelity term and the perimeter term of the Mumford-Shah functional. Numerical experiments show that, to the best of our knowledge, our method achieves the highest overall accuracy among fully unsupervised methods on three of the four standard benchmarks (Indian Pines, Kennedy Space Center, Pavia University and Salinas) evaluated on the full scenes. It also improves upon our previous Mumford-Shah based model.

authors.name: Benjamin Berkels
authors.institution: Aachen Institute for Advanced Study in Computational Engineering Science

papers.title: AdaptMIL: Domain Adaptation for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology
papers.abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) support a wide range of histopathology tasks on whole-slide images through multiple instance learning (MIL). Despite recent progress, these models remain sensitive to cross-hospital distribution shifts: performance often degrades when a task head (e.g., classification) is trained on data from one hospital and then used on data from another hospital. To address this challenge, we propose AdaptMIL, a training strategy for integrating domain adaptation into MIL training. AdaptMIL is motivated by our finding that directly applying domain adaptation objectives during MIL training can interfere with MIL aggregation learning, often resulting in performance degradation over standard training. AdaptMIL resolves this by decoupling representation-level domain alignment learning from MIL aggregation learning through a two-stage training procedure. We show that AdaptMIL improves cross-hospital performance and outperforms alternative adaptation methods across experiments spanning multiple WSI datasets, tasks, PFMs, MIL architectures, and domain adaptation objectives. AdaptMIL's code will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
papers.abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-γQ^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, γ>0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schrödinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.

papers.title: PULSE: Personalized Opportunistic Learning for Wearable Devices
papers.abstract: Wearable devices increasingly support personalized health and well-being applications, but post-deployment data can differ substantially from those used for training, while purely local adaptation may be limited by the data available on a single device during real-world operation. Conventional federated and decentralized learning rely on recurrent communication and stable connectivity, whereas existing opportunistic approaches often exploit available encounters without adequately considering their utility, compatibility, or communication cost. We propose PULSE, an event-driven framework for personalized opportunistic learning that treats each encounter as an online collaboration decision, selecting either no interaction or a promising nearby peer. Peer gradients are incorporated only when compatible with the local learning direction, while past interactions guide future peer selection. Across human activity recognition, fall detection, and stress recognition under synthetic and real contact traces, PULSE preserves or improves personalized classification performance, while reducing peer-assisted exchanges by 80-94% compared with opportunistic model averaging. On-device experiments further demonstrate its feasibility on wearable hardware: peer-assisted operations require limited energy, while the complete implementation occupies 149.8 KiB of RAM and 561.8 KiB of flash. The obtained results show that selective opportunistic collaboration can provide effective personalization while limiting communication and resource demands on constrained wearable devices.

papers.title: In PRAISE of Attributes: Grounding Retrieval Geometry with Query-Conditioned Subspaces for Person Re-Identification
papers.abstract: Person re-identification (ReID) ranks an image gallery using either an image query or a textual query. In image-to-image (I2I) ReID, viewpoint, illumination, occlusion, and background changes can make distractors appear more similar than the true match. In text-to-image (T2I) ReID, incomplete or ambiguous descriptions may omit key visual evidence. We study this problem for vision-language model (VLM) based ReID, where attributes such as clothing color and carried objects provide useful fine-grained matching cues. However, directly using attribute-prompt similarities as retrieval scores is unreliable because templated prompts can be biased, correlated, and poorly calibrated. We therefore propose \textbf{PR}ompt-guided \textbf{A}ttribute-based \textbf{I}nference-time \textbf{S}imilarity \textbf{E}nhancement (\texttt{PRAISE}), a query-side test-time adaptation framework for VLM-based ReID. Instead of treating prompts as scores, \texttt{PRAISE} uses a transferable attribute-prompt bank to construct an \emph{Attribute-Conditioned Subspace} (ACS): a query-dependent low-rank subspace induced by the most compatible attribute prompts. ACS provides a controlled attribute-conditioned geometry for reshaping query--gallery affinities and guiding lightweight inference-time updates without identity or attribute labels. Experiments across multiple I2I- and T2I-ReID benchmarks show that \texttt{PRAISE} consistently improves VLM retrieval backbones and outperforms both generic and ReID-specific TTA baselines.

papers.title: VVV CL001: A strong candidate for the most ancient star cluster in the Galaxy
papers.abstract: Finding the oldest globular cluster of the Galaxy is important to constrain a lower limit on the age of the Galaxy and the Universe. VVV CL001 ([l,b]= [5.26,0.77]) is perhaps the most metal-poor ([Fe/H]~-2.2 dex) globular cluster in the Galactic bulge and a promising candidate to be the oldest globular cluster in the entire Milky Way. Due to its recent discovery and high extinction, its physical parameters, especially the distance and age, remain highly uncertain, yet they are essential to define it as an ancient native stellar system of the Milky Way. We aim to refine the distance and age of VVV CL001 using deep and high-quality photometry, to study its role in the formation of the Milky Way, and to determine whether it is the oldest Galactic globular cluster. We used J and KS observations to construct the deepest CMD of VVV CL001 to date, based on FourStar/Baade PSF photometry combined with HST near-IR wide-filter PSF photometry. We selected cluster members through proper motion calculations and the HDBSCAN algorithm, and assigned membership probabilities via Markov-Chain Monte Carlo iterations in a 5-dimensional parameter space. Using r band data from DECam/Blanco, we optically identified horizontal branch members and applied an isochrone-fitting technique to determine the cluster distance, while members around the main-sequence turn-off yielded the age from different isochrone sets. Finally, we refined the cluster orbital parameters. We obtained a distance of d = 7.34 +- 0.46 kpc, the most precise to date. We derived an age of 13.4 +- 0.4 Gyr, indicating that VVV CL001 is one of the oldest globular clusters in the Galaxy. The orbit confirms that the cluster belongs to the Galactic bulge, which, together with its age and metallicity, could link it to the early proto-Milky Way assembly, extending the metal-poor end of the known in situ globular clusters.

authors.name: C. Quezada
authors.institution: Millennium Institute on Immunology and Immunotherapy

papers.title: Mean-field limit and Vlasov equation for a Gaussian-thermostatted Lorentz gas
papers.abstract: We study N particles moving in a dispersing billiard under an electric field and coupled through a Gaussian thermostat. The corresponding mean-field equation is a Vlasov-type equation with specular reflection. We reformulate the equation as a fixed point problem for the time-integrated thermostat coefficient. This yields existence of weak solutions for every absolutely continuous initial datum of finite energy and, for bounded initial densities supported on velocities that are large compared with the field, uniqueness of the weak solution; under the finite horizon assumption, the upper bound on the velocities can be replaced by an exponential tail of the initial density. In these regimes, we prove convergence of the empirical measures of the particle system to the solution of the kinetic equation. In general, convergence holds along subsequences.

papers.title: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties
papers.abstract: Trajectory tracking for compliant robots is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainties, often requiring learning-based methods to avoid explicit parameter identification. Iterative Learning Control (ILC) ensures theoretically high precision and preserves the passive compliance of the robot. However, traditional ILC requires a separate learning phase for each new trajectory. Conversely, Reinforcement Learning (RL) generalizes to new trajectories, but practically suffers from high sample complexity and limited tracking precision. This work proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC) that combines the strengths of both approaches to achieve fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories. By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials. In this architecture, ILC provides high-quality samples, while RL contributes as a generalizing best-effort policy across iterations. Additionally, a theoretical proof is presented to show that the RL component preserves ILC stability and, under specific conditions, can also reduce the error bound asymptotically. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on an underactuated 4-degree-of-freedom serial elastic robot using different trajectories and modeling mismatches.

papers.title: Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation predicts items by autoregressively generating semantic identifiers (SIDs), whose tokens are shared across semantically related items. With this paradigm gaining adoption, the question of how to support unlearning in it has become pressing. If training interactions must later be removed, such as injected spam or interactions with items a user no longer wants, this sharing lets an unlearning update unintentionally affect the predictions for the interactions' neighbors. We show that this effect is locally structured and hidden by global metrics: unlearning can leave recommendation utility on the whole test set nearly unchanged while substantially degrading it on neighborhoods of the forgotten interactions' SIDs. We propose Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning (NAU), which augments interaction-level unlearning with explicit control over the probability mass assigned to the forgotten items' neighborhoods. Across three datasets and four SID tokenizers, NAU restores spam-induced exposure toward the retrained reference while retaining more than 95% of retrained utility, and recovers the neighborhood utility that forget-and-repair unlearning loses at no global cost. We identify local probability redistribution as an important failure mode of unlearning in SID-based generative recommenders and show that explicitly controlling this redistribution can mitigate its effects.

authors.name: Pierre Lubitzsch
authors.institution: Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data

authors.name: Sebastian Schelter
