papers.abstract: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.

authors.name: Iván Angiono
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: A high-speed, large-aperture 3D printed laser shutter for cold atom experiments
papers.abstract: Cold atom experiments require optical shutters with rapid and repeatable actuation. Existing solutions often involve high cost, limited aperture diameter and slow transitioning. We present a 3D-printable shutter design featuring a large aperture of 4.5 mm diameter, low-cost assembly, and robust performance. The device achieves switching times of $399\pm8~μ$s with delays of $2.7\pm0.2$ ms for a fully illuminated aperture, with four different shutters demonstrating repeatable performance. We measure the shutter speed to be $7.0\pm0.1$ m/s. This approach offers an accessible, scalable solution for cold atom and other optical experiments requiring multiple shutters with precise light control and avoids the need to resize or precision-align a beam through an aperture.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Feedback on Handwritten Mathematics: Feedback Quality and Subsequent Exam Performance
papers.abstract: We evaluate the quality of feedback and practice exercises generated by GPT-5.1 from handwritten university mathematics answers and their grades, and examine whether receiving this feedback improves subsequent exam performance. We use six weekly bonus tests in an English (n=343) and a Dutch (n=236) cohort. Tests 1 and 3 used a crossover feedback design; otherwise, all attendees received feedback. To evaluate the feedback, six reviewers assessed 157 messages from three English-cohort tasks using six criteria scored from 0 to 3. The practice exercises received the highest proportion of strong ratings (95.5%), while diagnostic specificity (41.1%) and clarity and tone (33.4%) received fewer. Feedback for the lowest-scoring answers was rated as less actionable, suggesting that these students may need more targeted guidance from instructors. Comparisons of related exam questions showed mixed results, with no statistically significant differences after adjustment across four comparisons. Greater attendance and feedback exposure were associated with higher exam scores, but the contribution of feedback could not be separated from attendance and practice. Our findings show the potential of an integrated framework merging instructor guidance with automated feedback generation to provide personalised learning support at scale.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
papers.abstract: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.

papers.title: ARRIVAL in cube-root subexponential time
papers.abstract: In the ARRIVAL problem, a token travels through a switch digraph: at every vertex, it leaves along one of two out-arcs, and the two are used alternately. The question is which of two terminals the token reaches first. ARRIVAL lies in $\mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known.The fastest known algorithms turn some vertices into terminals and search for consistent guesses of the numbers of tokens that these vertices send out. The first, due to Gärtner et al. [ICALP 2021], searches all vertices at once with an algorithm for fixed points of monotone maps, and the second, due to Haslebacher [ICALP 2025], searches one vertex at a time by binary search. Both search for a fixed point of the same map, which returns how many tokens arrive at the guessed vertices. We guess the vertices in blocks of $k$, between these two extremes, which needs a search in $k$ dimensions with few evaluations of this map. To do so, we build on the connection between ARRIVAL and $\ell_1$-contractions established in the second of these works. We search with $\ell_1$-centerpoints of the remaining guesses, which are guaranteed to exist by Haslebacher et al. [FOCS 2025], and which we approximate deterministically. In order to prove our results, we show how to find the least fixed points of maps from $\{0, \ldots, N\}^k$ to itself that have unit increments. For ARRIVAL on $n$-vertex switch digraphs, this gives run time $2^{\mathcal{O}(n^{1/3} \cdot \log^{2/3} n)}$, improving the previous time bound of $n^{\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n})}$. We work with the more general \garrival problem, with many tokens and several terminals, and solve it in the same time when there are at most $2^n$ tokens.

authors.name: Raul Lopes
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: ORCA: Onboard Reflective Collaborative Agents for Reliable Task Offloading in LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites increasingly perform time-critical onboard processing, yet heterogeneous computing capabilities, rapidly changing inter-satellite links (ISLs) and uncertain neighbor behavior make decentralized task offloading difficult under partial observations. This paper presents ORCA, an architecture of Onboard Reflective Collaborative Agents for autonomous onboard task offloading. ORCA organizes offloading decisions into a four-Agent \emph{Perceive}$\rightarrow$\emph{Reason}$\rightarrow$ \emph{Act}$\rightarrow$\emph{Learn} loop. It aims to improve efficiency and reliability in dynamic, heterogeneous, and unreliable LEO satellite networks. The simulation results of a heterogeneous 60-satellite Walker-delta constellation demonstrates that ORCA delivers competitive system efficiency in cooperative settings while achieving superior task-success robustness and offloading reliability under previously unseen malicious node behavior, indicating that outcome-grounded reflection can improve the reliability of decentralized onboard offloading without centralized runtime coordination.

authors.name: Yunxin Geng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Shengxiang Hao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Weiwei Jiang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Building Telecom Language Models with RSOD: Domain Data, Specialist Post-Training, Memory-Conscious Distillation, and Networking Evaluation
papers.abstract: Telecom language models must combine broad networking knowledge with specialist behavior across routing, broadband services, access technologies, and operational diagnostics while remaining practical to deploy as a single model. We present an end-to-end framework that builds source-grounded synthetic training data from structured networking taxonomies and expert graphs, materializes 212,559 routed training records across fourteen networking routes, trains six frozen specialist LoRA teachers over one shared continued-pretrained backbone, and consolidates their behavior into one deployable student adapter using Routed Specialist On-Policy Distillation (RSOD). In RSOD, the committed student generates each trajectory, the route-assigned specialist teacher-forces the exact native token sequence, compact teacher hidden states are reconstructed through the shared frozen output head, and only the student LoRA is updated. A controlled reconstruction validation shows mean absolute logit error of 7.26 x 10^-6 with 100% top-1 agreement between native and reconstructed teacher logits. On four RTX 6000 Ada GPUs, the completed 2,000-step run produced 16,000 trajectories with zero observed student-version or token- ID mismatches. Under the primary route-conditioned evaluation over 2,850 held-out questions, the raw Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model scores 12.8661/25 micro (13.0172/25 macro), the combined routed six-teacher system scores 21.7641/25 micro, and the consolidated RSOD student, released as Llama-CalixCLM v1, reaches 21.7112/25 micro (21.8006/25 macro) on the same five dimension LLM-judge rubric. Under a separate neutral deployment-like prompt, the same student reaches 20.0028/25 micro (20.0778/25 macro). The consolidated student remains within 0.0529 micro-score points of the combined routed-teacher system while retaining a numerically validated and auditable train-serve execution path.

papers.title: Convolution Quadrature with Adaptive History Compression for Variable-Order Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a fully implicit fast method for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction--diffusion equations with periodic fractional diffusion and exponential-transition Scarpi memory. A Volterra-resolvent analysis establishes local well-posedness and temporal regularity estimates that describe the weak initial singularity. Backward Euler convolution quadrature combined with Fourier pseudospectral discretization achieves mesh-uniform stability and positive-time first-order convergence. To accelerate the scheme, we utilize Cauchy--FFT weight recovery and adaptive blockwise sum-of-exponentials compression, which significantly reduces the cost of history evaluation under local error control. A logarithmic perturbation bound quantifies the effects of weight recovery, history compression, and inexact nonlinear solves, giving tolerance conditions that preserve the convergence order. Numerical experiments confirm the first-order accuracy and demonstrate that the accelerated method efficiently resolves long-time spatial patterns at a substantially reduced computational cost.

authors.name: Pu Yuan
authors.institution: Anhui University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
papers.abstract: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract. We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. Kernel ridge regression with the trained NTK closely reproduces the network's predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel. Spectral analysis and multidimensional scaling reveal a geometry dominated by a small number of directions. Clustering and local neighborhood analysis organize compounds into recognizable superconducting families and connect materials with related chemical and correlated-electron properties despite substantial differences in $T_c$. These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.

authors.name: Gabriel Kotliar
authors.institution: Rutgers Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

papers.title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly participate in operational workflows where approvals, binds, and payments create commitments. An approval valid when issued may no longer authorize execution after relevant facts, evidence, policy, or authority change. We call this the evaluation--execution gap. We specify a state-bound runtime assurance layer that separates probabilistic measurement from deterministic adjudication, binds an execution allowance to the decision-relevant basis of an approval, invalidates that allowance after relevant logged changes, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch. This distinguishes the continued validity of a prior approval from a current-state policy check. We describe eight failure modes, an assurance model, a reference architecture, and prospective interventions with retrospective remediation. In a scripted 42-case replay, the state-bound configuration identifies 15 later-invalidated approvals that a deliberately non-re-evaluating point-in-time comparator does not revisit; it holds 14 affected actions before dispatch and compensates one landed effect. These results illustrate behavior under the stipulated policies and event orders, not superiority over dispatch-time enforcement designs or production effectiveness. Under explicit interception, ingestion, dependency, and serialization assumptions, the model establishes dispatch-time validity within the registered execution surface.

authors.name: Rajesh Gupta
authors.institution: Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust

papers.title: From Market Signals to Maintenance Decisions: Grid-Informed Maintenance Optimization in Offshore Wind Farms
papers.abstract: The reliable and cost-effective integration of large-scale offshore wind farms into power systems is largely influenced by maintenance operations. To date, power producers primarily rely on farm-level information (e.g., health signals, power generation, weather conditions) for maintenance planning of wind turbine fleets. We propose to consider additional grid-level information in maintenance operations, such as generation curtailment and market pricing. Periods of high generation curtailment or negative electricity pricing can be viewed as opportunities for preventive maintenance, since assets are fully or partially shut down due to grid-imposed constraints. We first analytically establish that access to market information has non-negative economic value for maintenance scheduling under a stylized setting, providing a theoretical foundation for treating market and grid information as a maintenance opportunity. We then formulate a grid-informed opportunistic maintenance scheduling model as a receding-horizon mixed integer linear program that jointly leverages both farm- and grid-level signals under realistic conditions to determine a maintenance plan for offshore wind turbines. Considering a 600-MW offshore wind farm in the United States, our proposed method reduces annual maintenance costs by up to 10%, while enhancing asset availability and resource utilization, relative to advanced maintenance models that solely rely on farm-level information.

authors.name: Robert Mieth
authors.institution: Rutgers Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

authors.name: Ahmed Aziz Ezzat
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: The GLEAM 4-Jy (G4Jy) Sample: V. Broadband spectral analysis
papers.abstract: The G4Jy Sample consists of 1,863 of the brightest sources in the southern sky, as selected at 151 MHz using the GaLactic and Extragalactic All-sky MWA (GLEAM) survey. We supplement existing, low-frequency radio data by completing visual inspection of radio images from the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS) at 887.5, 1367.5 and 1655.5 MHz. Doing so on a source-by-source basis allows us to assess the quality of the association of the radio emission, which we indicate via a flag system. Having multiple radio flux-densities allows us to construct broadband radio spectral energy distributions (SEDs), and these extend up to 20 GHz for sources that also have data from the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA). We fit polynomial functions to these SEDs, and determine the distribution of sources that are best-fit by absorption models, these accounting for 11 per cent of the sample. The SEDs are further modelled using the Radio AGN in Semi-analytic Environments (RAiSE) framework, for three assumed density-profiles (set by typical halo masses of 10^12.5, 10^13.5, and 10^14.5 Msol). The derived source ages show the expected distribution in the radio-power--size (P--D) diagram, whilst derived jet powers show non-linear behaviour. The latter is believed to be the result of higher densities, associated with higher magnetic fields, restricting the expansion of the radio jets/lobes.

authors.name: Siegfried A. Gawenda
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

authors.name: Joseph R. Callingham
authors.institution: Astronomical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Revisiting the Unknown Unknowns in Transient Astrophysics with the SKA Telescopes
papers.abstract: It was already recognised in the 2004 and 2014 SKA Science Case Chapters: "The Exploration of the Unknown" and "The SKA and the Unknown Unknowns", respectively, that the exploration of the unknown is an extremely important concept in realising the potential of any new instrument. This is especially true in an era of limited budgets but expanding analysis algorithms and capabilities. While this Chapter considers transients and environments, the ethos of these previous Chapters should be considered and embraced broadly and can be applied more broadly across SKAO science. We do not repeat in detail the important background these Chapters provide but encourage the reader to review them before reading this Chapter. In the last decade of radio transient astronomy, we have seen the value of these approaches with the expansion of the FRB population, the discovery of long period pulsars and transients and radio emission from white dwarfs to name just a few. With the SKAO, we should push the explored parameter space further and in new directions in all of the sensitivity, field-of-view, time, spectral, spectro-dynamic, polarisation and imaging domains. We should utilise approaches such as machine learning in allowing us to address the complexity that arises from the expanded parameter space and increased data rates and candidate sources. We will briefly summarise some of the impressive progress that the SKA pathfinders and precursors have made in these areas and what these mean for the SKA telescopes. We will also discuss ways in which it might be possible to push the current capabilities.

authors.name: J. Callingham
authors.institution: Astronomical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

authors.name: N. Hurley-Walker
authors.institution: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research

papers.title: On the LLM Verification for Argument Graph Generation
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems can formalize natural-language argumentation end-to-end, turning plain text into structured graphs by classifying components, connecting them with relations, and enriching the resulting graphs into formal models. Quality assurance for those graphs is almost always another LLMs: a reviewer, judge, or critic agent. On the other side, in adjacent neuro-symbolic fields, such generated output is often verified symbolically by external checks and solvers. In this work, we argue that in argument graph verification, the allocation should be similar, and based on what each instrument can guarantee. We propose layered verification: starting from deterministic checks, moving to solver-based and LLM reviews, and utilizing debate only under uncertainty, leaving human judgment for what no other instrument can decide. We ground our principle with a study on human-annotated graphs with injected structural defects. An LLM reviewer detects them at near-ceiling recall, including cycles in the support relation, but it objects to almost one in a ten correct graphs, even though it should not, happens to be inconsistent in verdict on identical inputs and is significantly slower than the equivalent exact check. It shows that while LLM reviewer does not lack the ability to detect structural defects, it is worth having a deterministic verification gates.

papers.title: New Directions in Irrationality
papers.abstract: Since Apéry's proof of the irrationality of $ζ(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Apéry as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $μ(ζ(2))<4.62675$ and $μ(ζ(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,ζ(3),ζ(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $μ(Aζ(3)+Bζ(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.

papers.title: BAIT: Can LLMs Find What Biases a Reader? A Benchmark for Cognitive Bias Triggers in News
papers.abstract: Persuasive writing exploits cognitive biases, recruiting a reader's mental shortcuts to shape belief, often without the reader noticing. We call the linguistic features exploiting such mental shortcuts cognitive bias triggers. As large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people encounter news, summarizing it, ranking it, and answering questions over it, a natural question is whether they can recognize the features of a text that bias a human reader. We introduce BAIT (Bias Annotation In Text), a resource for detecting cognitive bias triggers in news. BAIT pairs a schema of nine triggers, each specified in an annotator codebook, with 50 English news articles annotated by trained annotators at the article and span levels and adjudicated into a gold standard. On this data we define two tasks, detecting which triggers a text contains and locating the spans that carry them. We then benchmark six frontier LLMs zero-shot and with three or ten in-context examples. The models approach human agreement on which triggers an article contains, but rarely recover its full set of triggers, and they reach less than half of human agreement in locating the passages that carry them. Moreover, they over-predict triggers that come with easy surface cues, and most of the passages they mark for these triggers are not triggers, yet carry the trigger's surface cue far more often than random text. These findings suggest that the evaluated LLMs respond to surface cues rather than to the mechanisms that make a passage manipulative. We release the schema, the codebook, standoff annotations, and the evaluation pipeline.

papers.title: World Models with Configurable Perception
papers.abstract: Real-world observations are noisy and often contain excessive task-irrelevant information. Effective world modeling and planning need to abstract observations into world state representations while filtering out irrelevant information. However, encoders in existing world models are typically non-adaptive, leading to state representations that are easily distracted by task-irrelevant information. As a result, the model may not selectively filter observations to cater to different task demands. To address this problem, we introduce ConfigWM, which realizes configurable perception through task-conditioned state extraction. Given a language description of the task at hand, ConfigWM uses it as a configuration signal to steer how visual embeddings are mapped into a task-specific state space, selectively preserving information relevant to the current task while suppressing task-irrelevant variations. Action-conditioned dynamics are then learned in this task-specific state space for planning. We evaluate ConfigWM in environments with increasing levels of distraction. While existing methods exhibit substantial declines in planning success rate as the environments become increasingly noisy, ConfigWM remains comparatively stable and outperforms the strongest competing method by 22.3% on average across diverse environments. Consistent gains in physical-quantity probing (+0.365 Pearson r) and distracted-to-clean retrieval (+75.5%) further indicate that ConfigWM learns states that preserve task-relevant information while remaining robust to distractors, supporting reliable world modeling and planning in noisy worlds. Project Page: https://configwm.github.io

authors.name: Pascale Fung
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Improved Approximation and Hardness Results for the Monitoring Edge-Geodetic Set Problem
papers.abstract: We study the \emph{Monitoring Edge-Geodetic Set} problem (MEG-Set), which asks for a minimum-cardinality set $M$ of vertices of an undirected graph $G$ of $n$ vertices such that every edge of $G$ belongs to all shortest paths between some pair of vertices in $M$. We present new approximation and hardness results for MEG-Set. On the positive side, we design a deterministic polynomial-time $O(n^{1/3}\log^{2/3}n)$-approximation algorithm, improving upon the previously best-known $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ approximation ratio. On the negative side, for every constant $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, we prove that the problem admits no polynomial-time $\big(2^{\log^{1-\varepsilon} n}\big)$-approximation algorithm, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq \mathsf{DTIME}(n^{\operatorname{polylog} n})$. This substantially improves upon the previously known logarithmic inapproximability bound. We also prove that \megset is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard on planar $2$-degenerate graphs, whereas $\mathsf{NP}$-hardness was previously known for $1$-apex $2$-degenerate graphs. We conclude by observing a connection between monitoring edge-geodetic sets and subsetwise distance preservers, i.e., subgraphs that preserve distances between all pairs of vertices in $S\subseteq V(G)$. Specifically, we show that any upper bound on the size of the latter yields a lower bound on the size of the former.

papers.title: Slowly Rotating Fully Convective Stars at $\lesssim$ 1 Gyr: Evidence from the Hyades and Praesepe
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of 10 stars in the Praesepe and Hyades clusters with unusually slow rotation that are likely not field contamination. Even though our search was general, all slow rotators are in the fully convective domain. We find that the fraction of slow rotators in the clusters is more than $5σ$ above the distribution expected from field contamination. They provide a potential link between the period distribution of the young open clusters and the field. These stars could be a distinct birth population, or they could be an indication that the onset of strong magnetic breaking is earlier than previously realized in this domain. Photometric variability and X-ray luminosity suggest the later but more data is needed to confirm. Searches for similar populations in younger clusters will help determine when slow rotators first emerge and constrain the timescale and physical mechanisms governing angular-momentum loss in fully convective stars. The discovery of these stars also highlights the importance of long-baseline photometric observations for detecting the long rotation periods of low-mass stars.

authors.name: Guy S. Stringfellow
authors.institution: Astronomical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Emergent Active-Blob Length Scale Governs the Collapse Transition of Tangentially Driven Polymers
papers.abstract: The coil-to-globule transition is a paradigmatic phenomenon in polymer physics and biophysics, in which polymer chains evolve from swollen to globular conformations upon decreasing solvent quality. At equilibrium, this transition can be rationalized in terms of a thermal blob length that diverges at the so-called $Θ$ condition, marking the crossover from self-avoiding to globular conformations. How activity modifies this conformational transition and affects the fundamental length scales at play remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question for tangentially driven polymers using Brownian dynamics simulations, systematically varying both intrachain attraction strength and activity. We find that polar activity smears out the crossover from swollen to globular conformations. Between self-avoiding and $Θ$ conditions, activity dominates by introducing an emergent folding length scale, which acts as an active blob length. In this regime, we demonstrate that the ratio of thermal to active length scales provides a new scaling variable that leads to a universal master curve for active polymer collapse.

papers.title: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of agent harnesses has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents. By searching the harness space for a specific LLM on a given dataset, RSI can discover a harness tailored to the capabilities and behavioral characteristics of that model. However, such optimization often creates a strong coupling between the learned harness and its target LLM, limiting generalization across models and requiring substantial computational resources to adapt to new LLMs. Moreover, existing RSI methods typically optimize a harness using feedback from a single model and evaluate its generalization to other models only after training. This paradigm treats model differences primarily as a criterion for evaluating generalization rather than as valuable evidence for optimization. In this paper, we introduce a new perspective that treats models as data and places the harness at the center of optimization. Building on this perspective, we propose \textsc{MaD-RSI}, a framework that directly optimizes a shared harness across multiple heterogeneous LLMs by incorporating their diverse failure trajectories into the training process. Rather than assessing model differences only after optimization, \textsc{MaD-RSI} leverages these differences as training evidence to guide the self-improvement of a shared harness. Furthermore, we introduce a new evaluation framework with two complementary metrics designed to assess the effectiveness of harness optimization across models. Experiments across multiple datasets and LLMs demonstrate that \textsc{MaD-RSI} improves generalization over existing approaches while reducing training costs.

authors.name: Yu Cui
authors.institution: École nationale des ponts et chaussées

papers.title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
papers.abstract: Momentum is central to stochastic optimization in deep learning, including the training of large language models. Classical momentum methods typically rely on a fast exponential moving average (EMA) scheme, which discounts past gradients on a fixed timescale and may underweight older gradients that remain informative. This creates a trade-off between retaining long-term history and adapting to recent changes. We introduce Hybrid Momentum (HyM), which combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum. The former assigns weights proportional to the gradients' iteration indices and retains a growing span of history, while the latter emphasizes recent gradients. This hybrid construction is modular and can be combined with adaptive preconditioning and other update transformations. In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales. Across image classification, machine translation, and language modeling, HyM and HyMUON match or improve upon strong baselines. HyMUON improves over Muon on IWSLT14, and in both the 100k- and 600k-step GPT-2 124M OpenWebText regimes. For LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.

authors.name: Chenyu Zhou
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
papers.abstract: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.

papers.title: Distributed Platoon Control for Safe and Smooth Crossing at an Unsignalized Intersection-Part I: Stability Analysis
papers.abstract: We propose a distributed platoon controller that guarantees safe and smooth crossing of multi-vehicle systems at an unsignalized intersection. To support the stability analysis, we consider a multi-vehicle platoon maneuvering along a closed path with a single unsignalized intersection. Unlike traditional bi-level decoupled designs on open paths, which primarily focus on intersection control while neglecting its coupling with platoon convergence, and thus hindering rigorous convergence analysis, the closed-path setting allows us to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the platoon. The local exponential convergence analysis of the switched closed-loop system, induced by repeated vehicle switching at the intersection, is presented. Under some mild conditions on the controller gains, we show that safe intersection crossing is ensured during the transient phase and smooth crossing is achieved in steady state, where all vehicles travel at a common constant speed while avoiding collisions at the intersection. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed distributed controller is demonstrated in a high-fidelity CARLA simulator using multiple commercial vehicle models.

authors.name: Shuwei Pei
authors.institution: Chinese Research Academy of Environmental Sciences

papers.title: KPHarness: Co-Evolving Knowledge and Probing for Long-Horizon Gaming Harnesses
papers.abstract: A failed gaming trajectory reveals that an agent needs intervention, but not necessarily how its execution harness should change. Effective harness adaptation therefore requires gathering diagnostic evidence, rather than merely proposing alternative recovery rules. We present KPHarness, a framework that adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model through knowledge-probing co-evolution. Recovery knowledge supplies context-specific intervention hypotheses that guide active probing; probe outcomes reveal when these hypotheses apply and provide evidence for refining both recovery knowledge and later probe selection. This reciprocal process allows the harness to improve not only which interventions it applies, but also how it investigates failures. KPHarness separates fast policy execution from a slow research loop that translates accumulated knowledge and probing evidence into bounded harness revisions. Each revision is compared with the incumbent under matched sandbox conditions and accepted only when the paired evaluation shows improvement. Recoveries supported by further validation are retained for cross-task reuse, while immediate interaction feedback and delayed episode-success credit update action- and knowledge-probing policies during adaptation. Experiments on Minecraft tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting show improved task coverage over bare policy execution, a manually specified fixed harness, and knowledge-only harness evolution with non-adaptive probing. Evaluation on previously unseen tasks further shows improved task completion with the evolved harness, knowledge bank, and probing policies held fixed,

authors.name: Sen Cui
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

papers.title: Bayesian Neural Networks via Dirichlet Process Priors on the Data-Generating Distribution for Randomized Value Functions in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) offer a principled framework for quantifying epistemic uncertainty. However, standard weight-space priors yield complex, high-dimensional neural network posteriors that are computationally prohibitive to sample from, and popular approximate inference schemes often fail to capture epistemic uncertainty effectively---a failure mode particularly acute in reinforcement learning (RL) \citep{osband2018randomized}. To resolve this challenge, we introduce a new class of BNNs that quantify uncertainty by placing Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet Process (DP) priors directly on the underlying data-generating distribution rather than on network parameters. Building on this foundation, we develop DP-DQN, a reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages DP-BNNs to maintain posterior distributions over value functions and perform efficient Thompson sampling. By grounding randomized value functions in Bayesian nonparametrics, DP-DQN unifies data-driven posterior reweighting (via the Bayesian Bootstrap) with generative prior hypotheses injected directly through the DP base measure, enabling decisive ``deep exploration'' with a single neural network without the overhead of multi-network ensembles.

authors.name: Sumit Vashishtha
authors.institution: Centre de Recherche en Informatique, Signal et Automatique de Lille

papers.title: How Developers Configure LLM Inference: A Large-Scale Study of Real-World Practices
papers.abstract: LLMs are increasingly integrated into software systems, making deployment and inference configuration a recurring software engineering task. Inference backends expose many options that affect model loading, generation, serving, and request processing. Yet little is known about which of these options developers explicitly configure in practice. In this paper, we present a large-scale empirical study of LLM inference configuration practices in open-source software using Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and the OpenAI API. We analyze 5,398 GitHub repositories using at least one of these backends and identify 345,117 explicitly configured option occurrences. Our results show that developers use only a small part of the available configuration space regularly. Although 98.8% of the documented backend-specific options appear at least once, 78.9% are configured in at most 10% of repositories using the corresponding backend. Configurations are also small, with a median of 2 options for Transformers and 4 for vLLM and OpenAI, but the combinations of options vary widely: 56.8-61.6% of multi-option signatures appear in only one repository. We also observe recurring option values as well as substantial variation in how values are chosen. Finally, configuration practices differ across application contexts, with option-adoption differences reaching 30.7 percentage points. These findings characterize the configuration surface developers make explicit rather than the importance or optimality of individual options. They provide empirical evidence for prioritizing future studies of inference configuration and for improving backend documentation and configuration support.

authors.name: Romain Rouvoy
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université de Lille

papers.title: 2-representation theory of the Taft algebra
papers.abstract: We study the $2$-representation theory of the Taft category, the tensor category of finite-dimensional modules over the Taft algebra. This category has two left cells. We first classify suitable transitive modules over its based representation ring. For the upper cell, we recall a construction by Etingof and Ostrik giving an infinite family of pairwise nonequivalent simple $2$-representations. For the bottom cell, we pass to the semisimplification of the Taft category and identify a distinguished fusion subcategory with an adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Verlinde category. Using algebra objects associated with $\mathsf{ADET}$-diagrams and categorical Clifford theory, we classify the regular exact indecomposable module categories of this semisimplification. For these regular module categories, the split Grothendieck group is a complete invariant. Finally, we identify the two cell $2$-representations of the Taft category.

papers.title: UvA-MT's Participation in the WMT26 General Translation Shared Task
papers.abstract: This paper presents UvA-MT's submission to the WMT 2026 General Machine Translation shared task, competing in the unconstrained track across all 23 translation directions. This year, we fully leverage the test-time methods of Large Language Models (LLMs) for machine translation. Specifically, (1) we use sequential sampling with a refinement prompt to generate a pool of translation candidates for each source segment, a strategy shown to outperform traditional parallel sampling; and (2) we employ LLMs as pairwise judges to select the best candidate via a round-robin voting mechanism, with offline evaluation on the WMT25 benchmark showing a very clear improvement over point-wise best-of-N selection. Combined, these two strategies form our WMT26 submission.

authors.name: Di Wu
authors.institution: Lanzhou Institute of Husbandry and Pharmaceutical Sciences

papers.title: SPAR: Search-trained Push Action Ranker for Efficient Navigation Among Movable Obstacles
papers.abstract: Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) requires a robot to rearrange objects that block access to its goal. For a pushing robot, progress may depend on a setup push that enables a later opening without itself clearing a passage. The number of candidate sequences can grow exponentially with sequence length, making physics-based search costly. We introduce the Search-trained Push Action Ranker (SPAR), which learns to prioritize push primitives from simulated search outcomes. Searches over sequences of up to two pushes per object provide supervision that distinguishes immediate openings from setup pushes. A transformer trained with regression and ranking losses scores primitives using contact tokens conditioned on scene geometry and reachability regions. The same model guides simulator evaluations in SPAR Search and selects actions for direct execution in SPAR Policy. Both modes solve successive keyhole problems that open access to neighboring free-space regions within a NAMO planner. Across successful runs on $300$ simulated two-push keyhole problems, SPAR Search reduces median simulator calls by $7.0\times$, leading to a $3.8\times$ reduction in planning time relative to Random Search. Without retraining, the same ranker guides search on $600$ keyhole problems which have no solution within two pushes. At a depth limit of five pushes, SPAR Search achieves $50.7\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $20.2\%$ for Random Search. These gains carry over to NAMO planning: on hard simulated scenes, SPAR Search achieves $47\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $21\%$ for Random Search. In real-robot experiments, SPAR Policy succeeds in $37/40$ trials without a physics-based digital twin, compared with $33/40$ for SPAR Search and $27/40$ for Random Search.

authors.name: Dhruv Metha Ramesh
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Junshan Huang
authors.institution: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Jingjin Yu
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Abdeslam Boularias
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Generalizing Multimodal Foundational Models in Context-Driven Class Incremental Learning
papers.abstract: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to learn new classes continuously without forgetting the previously learned ones. Recent works in CIL have significantly advanced across various modalities; however, at the intersection of audio-visual modality, this problem remains underexplored. While representations from multimodal foundational models (MFMs) encapsulate rich static priors, our preliminary analysis shows that these representations struggle in incremental settings. Motivated by this, we propose a framework that generalizes frozen MFMs to audio-visual CIL. Specifically, we leverage their dense audio and visual representations and employ an attention-based contextual guidance module, in which the audio representations serve as task-stable contextual guidance for the visual representations, enabling effective class recognition in the incremental setting. To further mitigate catastrophic forgetting and preserve stability across tasks, we employ feature- and logit-level distillation, which are primarily responsible for the reduced forgetting. Extensive evaluations across various audio-visual CIL benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at https://github.com/avigupta2798/MFM-CIL.

authors.name: Tammam Tillo
authors.institution: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi

papers.title: Complete Street Design informed by Multi-Agent Simulation
papers.abstract: Objectives: Complete Street design is currently guided largely by qualitative principles despite the increasing complexity of multimodal urban traffic. This paper develops a microscopic simulation framework for quantitatively evaluating alternative street designs by explicitly representing heterogeneous road users, including Autonomous Vehicles (AVs), Connected Vehicles (CVs), Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs), pick-up and drop-off (PUDO) services, and micromobility users. The framework jointly evaluates mobility and safety within a unified testbed. Methods:The framework enriches microscopic simulation with behavioral models for heterogeneous road users. It explicitly captures lateral movements, parking maneuvers, pedestrian crossings and jaywalking, and shared-lane bicycle and scooter interactions. Safety is quantified using a conflict severity measure grounded in collision physics, while candidate street layouts are optimized using a genetic algorithm. Findings: Applied to a segment of Belmont Avenue in Chicago, Illinois, the framework shows that dedicated bicycle lanes reduce conflict severity at the expense of vehicular throughput. Increasing AV penetration mitigates congestion by reducing traffic shockwaves while improving interactions with pedestrians relative to CVs and HDVs. The optimization framework efficiently identifies Pareto-efficient street layouts that balance mobility and safety. Novelty: The proposed framework integrates heterogeneous behavioral modeling, physics-based conflict assessment, stochastic performance evaluation, and design optimization within a single quantitative framework for Complete Street design. Practical Applications: The framework provides transportation planners with a predictive virtual testbed for evaluating street designs and quantifying the tradeoff between mobility and safety before implementation.

authors.name: Nie
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: DeHNSSo-v2: A compressible, curvilinear, and efficient extension of the Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver
papers.abstract: We present DeHNSSo-v2, a major update of DeHNSSo-v1 (Westerbeek et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 302, 2024), the open-source Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver for nonlinear stability analysis of shear flows. The new release adds a compressible formulation on general two-dimensional body-fitted geometries, automatic grid generation, linear-cost sparse assembly, reusable per-mode factorizations, and Newton pseudo-arclength continuation for high-amplitude nonlinear solutions. The curvilinear formulation preserves the fourth-order accuracy of the discretization on strongly distorted grids, and the compressible solver is confirmed to reproduce DeHNSSo-v1 in the incompressible limit. Validation spans published benchmarks for linear instability of compressible flat-plate boundary layers from $\mathrm{Ma}=0.5$ to $\mathrm{Ma}=4.5$, nonlinear oblique-mode breakdown at $\mathrm{Ma}=1.6$, nonlinear swept-wing crossflow compared with direct numerical simulations, and linear Tollmien-Schlichting wave interaction with a modeled surface-embedded Helmholtz resonator compared with experimentally validated linearized Navier-Stokes simulations. On the nonlinear test cases of DeHNSSo-v1, the computational developments result in a speed-up of approximately one order of magnitude. By broadening the scope and reducing the cost of DeHNSSo-v1, DeHNSSo-v2 provides the boundary-layer-transition and flow-control community with an accessible tool for studying receptivity, nonlinear disturbance evolution, and instability interactions with complex surface geometry and metamaterials across compressibility regimes.

papers.title: TexFlow: learning crystallographic texture on SO(3) manifold via normalizing flows
papers.abstract: Crystallographic texture is an important microstructural feature that statistically describes the orientations of grains in polycrystalline materials. Conventional texture analysis relies on the orientation distribution functions and pole figures, which are essential for interpreting the texture of a given material specimen but do not, by themselves, provide a direct framework for predictive modeling of process-structure-property linkages. Data- and machine learning-based approaches offer a means to address this gap; however, a key challenge lies in developing representations and learning frameworks that account for the manifold structure of rotations. In particular, many existing machine learning techniques are designed for Euclidean data and therefore are not readily applicable to rotations in the non-Euclidean group $\text{SO}(3)$. Here we introduce TexFlow, a conditional normalizing flow framework for texture modeling that learns a probability distribution over rotations in $\text{SO}(3)$ by construction. Rotations are encoded in a six-dimensional Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization representation which is then mapped back to valid rotations $\mathbf{R}\in\text{SO}(3)$. The framework supports conditional probabilistic modeling of texture $p(\mathbf{R}|c)$, where $c$ may represent processing parameters like temperature or deformation state. To complement conventional texture-analysis visualizations, such as pole figures and sections of the orientation distribution function, we further introduce Hopf-fibration visualizations as a compact global representation of texture. TexFlow is validated on both unconditional and conditional experimental and simulated texture datasets spanning diverse material systems. We show that TexFlow can accurately capture multimodal textures and their conditional evolution, providing a data-driven framework for establishing process-texture linkages.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
papers.abstract: We establish Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary fractional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system with different orders of dissipation. Our first result shows that every smooth solution satisfying the natural homogeneous Sobolev energy conditions is trivial whenever $1\leqα\leq 5/3$ and $3\leqα+2β\leq5$, without any additional integrability assumptions on the velocity or magnetic fields. This extends previous results to new parameter regimes, including cases with $β<1$. Beyond this region, we prove a complementary Liouville theorem under suitable integrability conditions only on the radial components of the velocity and magnetic fields. The proofs rely on the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and localized energy estimates.

authors.name: Gaston Vergara-Hermosilla
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry

papers.title: Confessions of a Masked MDP
papers.abstract: In reinforcement learning, one presumes the action set to be known ahead of time, and, thus, one must know if any state-action pairs are not permissible ahead of computations. In some applications, determining this action mask is the main computational bottleneck. Isolating this problem to highlight its core properties, we study how to combine the search for an optimal policy with the learning of the mask itself, under a linear MDP model in which each attempted action reveals the exact value of a linear score determining its validity. In this framework, we first construct an algorithm based on deterministic optimistic optimization and show that it is minimax optimal, which we show is also computationally efficient. However, it is sub-optimal on non-degenerate instances, as we show. We propose an alternative, which is also computationally efficient, which plans its exploration strategy. This algorithm admits a formal interpretation as an analogue of information-directed-sampling for deterministic feedback, which may be of independent interest. Finally, we study an application of this framework to transfer learning, where the invalid action set changes over time.

authors.name: Lorenzo Croissant
authors.institution: Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique

papers.title: Front-pinned spectral collocation for the flame problem and related ignition problems
papers.abstract: We consider global Chebyshev collocation for the ignition problems $y'=y^q(1-y)$, $y(0)=δ$, $q\ge2$; for $q=2$ this is the flame problem, a standard stiff test equation. After rescaling to $[-1,1]$ the solution has an interior layer of width $O(μ)$, $μ=(q-1)δ^{q-1}$, at a $δ$-dependent position. Two obstacles arise: plain Chebyshev collocation needs $O(1/μ)$ nodes, and imposing the initial condition amplifies errors by a factor of order $1/μ$, which makes the collocation equations severely ill-conditioned. Our main contribution addresses the second one. Since all solutions are translates of one profile, the initial condition can be replaced by an equivalent interior condition. For an unknown $u=\varphi(y)$, imposing it where the speed $|\varphi'f_q|$ of $u$ along the orbit is maximal bounds the propagator of the linearized equation by one; for $u=\ln y$ this is $y(x^\ast)=(q-1)/q$. For the first obstacle we use the sinh map of Tee and Trefethen: the time function is explicit, the complex singularities of the profile lie exactly at $\pm(2k+1)πi$, and the map parameters follow in closed form, so that $O(\ln(1/μ))$ nodes suffice. In double precision the pinned scheme reaches the interpolation error of the exact solution in five or six Newton iterations for $μ$ down to $10^{-12}$, whereas the initial-condition form fails or converges to wrong discrete solutions, also in an integral (Birkhoff) reformulation. Computations in $256$-bit arithmetic confirm the predicted rate down to errors of $10^{-70}$, AAA approximation locates the singularities to within $2\%$, and the method carries over to an Arrhenius reaction rate, with all parameters computed numerically.

papers.title: KoalaGS: Complexity-Aware Continuous Level of Detail for Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Deploying a trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scene under shrinking compute budgets requires one primitive set to remain effective when rendered at smaller prefixes. In this continuous level of detail (LoD) setting, the challenge is to decide which Gaussians should retain capacity as the budget decreases. A pilot study on 3DGS-MCMC reconstructions shows that image complexity, computed from the input views before optimization, predicts where reconstruction error concentrates in image and 3D space. It also reveals that simple regions contain too many Gaussians and degrade as much as complex ones at lower budgets, despite being inherently cheaper to represent. Subsequently, in KoalaGS, during training we use this complexity prior to bias relocation toward poorly reconstructed areas while ensuring smooth degradation across LoDs. A primitive importance score then enables inference at low-capacity, while preserving the scene structure. Tested across three datasets, KoalaGS maintains competitive full-capacity quality while significantly improving quality across the budget spectrum, yielding smoother transitions across LoDs, and enabling faster progressive streaming.

papers.title: Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
papers.abstract: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.

authors.name: Rebecca L. Dally
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.name: J. W. Lynn
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
papers.abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $τ$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $τ-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronquée solution of Painlevé I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $β=2$ random band matrices.

authors.name: Pierre Le Doussal
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Nanoscale chemical engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers through in situ electron beam irradiation in a TEM
papers.abstract: Defect engineering in low-dimensional materials is a powerful approach to tailor their structure and chemistry at the atomic scale, with high relevance for tuning physical properties. Here, we apply this strategy to MXenes, one of the largest families of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and demonstrate the use of a highly focused scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) beam for the structural and chemical nanoengineering of titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) multilayers. By adjusting the beam energy, electron dose, and scanning parameters, Ti3C2Tx multilayers were irradiated at 80 and 300 keV and characterized in situ using annular dark-field imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS). The irradiation induces gradual structural and chemical modifications, largely driven by the selective sputtering of atomic species and MXene layers. We identify irradiation conditions that selectively remove Cl or F surface terminations while largely preserving the Ti3C2 framework, whereas other conditions promote preferential carbon removal, in agreement with theoretical predictions. Most notably, electron irradiation drives the migration and accumulation of initially dilute nitrogen impurities within the irradiated regions, leading to the formation of nitrogen-rich titanium carbonitride (Ti3CyNzTx) nanodomains embedded in the Ti3C2Tx multilayers. These laterally patterned carbide/carbonitride architectures constitute in-plane MXene heterostructures with nanometer-scale spatial control. These results demonstrate that electron irradiation can be used to locally tailor MXene composition and create nanoscale architectures beyond those accessible through conventional chemical synthesis.

authors.name: Ayoub Benmoumen
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
