papers.title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.

authors.name: Peng Gao
authors.institution: Institut des Hautes Études de Tunis

papers.title: Controlling exceptional points of layered non-Hermitian structures with magnetic field
papers.abstract: Exceptional points are the characteristic features of non-Hermitian systems providing numerous applications in optics, acoustics, electronics, etc. We show that exceptional points can be controlled with the external magnetic field by considering the archetypal three-layered $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric photonic structure including a magneto-optic material between the loss and gain layers. Application of the magnetic field makes the system anisotropic with the polarization-sensitive reflection and transmission properties. As a result, the magnetic field can stimulate $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry breaking and mode exchange at realistic values of system parameters. Moreover, we suggest that the proposed scheme can be also used for magnetic-perturbation sensing with an easily adaptable level of desired field strength. Our results contain a valuable evidence for the usefulness of anisotropic (including magnetic) materials for tunable non-Hermitian photonics.

papers.title: Less is More: Concise Retrieval and Critic-based Re-ranking for Composed Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Zero-shot composed image retrieval (ZS-CIR) aims to retrieve a target image based on a reference image and modification text. Recent approaches commonly rely on large vision-language models to generate target image captions for retrieval. However, these captions may include redundant semantic details, introducing noise when retrieving the target image and leading to suboptimal retrieval results. To address this issue, we propose Less-is-More CIR, a two-stage training-free framework that combines Concise Retrieval and Critic Re-ranking. In the first stage, concise target-oriented captions are generated that preserve only the most discriminative modification semantics, thereby reducing semantic noise in the retrieval. In the second stage, a critic re-rank module further evaluates the retrieved candidates from the perspectives of modification consistency and reference preservation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework for the ZS-CIR. Our code is available at: https://github.com/dxlabskku/LM-CIR.

authors.name: Yuqian Zheng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: DeGroot Dynamics on Multiplex Networks with Directed and Acyclic Interlayer Connectivities
papers.abstract: In models of opinion dynamics, researchers typically examine how an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced by the opinions of their neighbors in a network. However, people's opinions on a topic are also influenced by their opinions and their neighbors' opinions on related topics. In an election, for example, the opinions of a voter on a variety of issues inform their opinions of electoral candidates. To consider the influence between people's opinions on multiple distinct topics, we study a multiplex extension of the traditional DeGroot consensus model. In our multiplex DeGroot model, different network layers represent distinct topics and directed interlayer edges (which are not allowed to form cycles) encode relationships between distinct topics. In our model, an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced both by the opinions of their neighbors on that topic and by their own opinions on related topics. We prove under mild conditions that our multiplex DeGroot model converges to a limit state. We also prove that strong connectedness in ``source layers'' (which represent fundamental beliefs) eventually yields a consensus opinion in each layer. In particular, we show that consensus on source layers can lead to consensus on other layers even when those layers otherwise would be polarized. By numerically simulating our multiplex DeGroot model on a two-layer network, we examine the effects on opinion dynamics of (1) different network structures and (2) different types of initial opinion data.

papers.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
papers.abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

papers.title: Knowledge as Code
papers.abstract: For millennia, knowledge has been carried by language, and large language models still put language at the center. Yet the coding agents built on these models mostly write code. This paper is a contribution to epistemology, which asks what kind of knowledge code is and how it is obtained. We define knowledge as code as knowledge written in a programming language or in a machine-parsable data format, whose validity can be checked by executing it. We define thirteen epistemic properties of knowledge media and show that code is the first medium to have all of them. We distinguish two ways in which knowledge enters code, encoding and learning by execution, where code is both the experiment and the record of its result. Agents make learning by execution observable, since their trajectories record every probe, observation and line of code they keep. Code is thus not only a tool of knowledge work but a knowledge medium in its own right, the first that can check what it holds.

papers.title: Reading Too Much Into It? Interpretive Preferences and Commitment in LLM Mentalisation under Ambiguity
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for interpersonal advice, potentially shaping how users interpret ambiguous social encounters. Existing Theory of Mind evaluations typically rely on predefined answers, while uncertainty research overlooks LLMs' preferred explanations and confidence under psychological distress. To address these gaps, we introduce MentalLoom, a novel evaluation of LLM mentalisation comprising 604 ambiguous social episodes, matched depression and social anxiety disclosures, and four-turn dialogues with unchanged event evidence. Across eight LLMs, disclosures initially elicited more negative explanations overall but more positive narrator-directed interpretations. Scripted repeated questioning showed greater emotional support, stronger positive narrator-directed endorsement, and higher certainty without new event evidence. These findings show that user context can reshape interpretive preferences and commitment while the underlying ambiguity remains unresolved.

authors.name: Yaling Shen
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiangyu Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Curriculum Learning for Generative Flexible Docking
papers.abstract: Flexible docking is a highly practical task, aiming to predict the joint configuration of a protein-ligand complex from a protein apo structure and a ligand SMILES string. Diffusion and flow-based generative models have made this task tractable by modeling the posterior distribution over the ligand pose and the protein conformation conditioned on the apo input. The central challenge, however, remains the long-tailed apo-to-holo structure shift, where a small fraction of protein undergo large conformational changes. In this work, motivated by the practical observation that downweighting large shift examples improves generalization, and by the mixed nature of the long tail consisting of genuinely difficult examples and noisy ones, we propose to use curriculum learning for this task, gradually incorporating large conformational change examples during training. With a linear pacing function, we show that an existing method can be strongly enhanced. On the PDBBind ESMFold apo benchmark, with relaxation and confidence-based pose selection, the resulting model GCLDock achieves a 46.52% top-1 success rate (ligand RMSD less than 2A) and 40.26% when additionally requiring PoseBusters validity, outperforming existing baselines.

papers.title: Lower bounds for Bayesian CVaR in interactive problems with local differential privacy
papers.abstract: We develop an information-theoretic method for lower bounding the prior-predictive conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of loss in interactive statistical decision making (ISDM). A generalized Fano inequality replaces a single error event by a randomized binary statistic constructed from a bounded transform of the loss, reducing the problem to a Bernoulli $f$-divergence inequality. A bounded hinge transform yields a direct lower bound on Bayesian CVaR under a prior fixed in advance. We derive reverse-KL specializations and obtain explicit bounds for Gaussian mean estimation and Gaussian stochastic bandits. We then impose local differential privacy (LDP) at the observation stage of the same ISDM model. LDP contraction inequalities combined with the adaptive KL chain rule give explicit Bayesian CVaR lower bounds for Gaussian mean estimation with heterogeneous privacy parameters and Gaussian $K$-armed bandits.

papers.title: Worst-Case Bayesian CVaR Regret Bounds for Episodic Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: We study the worst-case, over priors, Bayesian conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of cumulative pseudo-regret in time-homogeneous finite-horizon episodic Markov decision processes. A high-probability guarantee for UCBVI-BF yields a prior-predictive upper bound. A lower bound follows by a three-state MDP and applying a reverse-KL inequality. For a constant number of states, the bounds have the same polynomial dependence on horizon, actions, and episodes, with a logarithmic gap in the risk level.

papers.title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation is increasing the demand for accurate forecasting across large numbers of geographically dispersed stations. Existing approaches are commonly developed for individual sites or specific forecasting horizons, requiring repeated training and maintenance as new stations are integrated and limiting direct reuse at previously unseen sites. To address this scalability gap, this paper presents a domain-specific foundation-style pretraining framework that learns a shared forecasting model from heterogeneous multi-site and multi-horizon PV data. NWP-assisted forecasting is formulated as a sequence-completion problem that unifies historical PV power, meteorological observations, future numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecasts, and time encodings. Three pretraining objectives are designed and systematically evaluated, including forecast-aligned reconstruction, generic reconstruction, and mixed reconstruction. The mixed objective combines the operational structure of PV forecasting with random sequence reconstruction and provides the most balanced performance across forecasting accuracy, degraded NWP conditions, and downstream adaptation. Experiments on 479 distributed PV stations use 340 stations for model development and 139 spatially held-out stations for zero-shot evaluation. Across horizons from 6 hours to 7 days, the multi-site pretrained MR model outperforms representative station-specific and shared baselines, as well as generalist time-series models, including a recent large-scale pretrained foundation model. The pretrained model can also be directly deployed at new PV stations and subsequently adapted to region-specific operational objectives when local data become available, providing a scalable forecasting paradigm for large distributed PV fleets.

authors.name: Shibo Zhu
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

papers.title: Learned Readout Tokens for Extracting Large Language Model Confidence
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used within everyday applications where their responses have significant downstream impacts. For responsible deployment of such systems, we desire insight into how much we can trust their individual outputs. A popular approach for estimating LLM confidence is to train probes on the hidden states of the LLM's tokens to predict the correctness of the model's output. These probes typically read hidden states from tokens that are already in the model's vocabulary. In this work, we introduce a new approach to confidence probes that learn a new readout token and utilize its hidden states to train the probe. We show that our learned readout approach ScratchProbe outperforms its existing-token counterpart on a variety of datasets and LLMs. We also extend our method to a multi-token approach which we show provides further performance improvements. Finally, since the learned readout changes only the position a probe reads from, any existing probe can adopt it. Applied to a state-of-the-art probe, it improves AUROC on every backbone, in domain and out of domain.

papers.title: When Does Hate Transfer? A Large-Scale Study of Cross-Lingual Hate Speech Detection
papers.abstract: Effective detection of hate content is essential for maintaining healthy online communities, yet performance can vary substantially across languages. This work investigates a core practical question: Can training data from one language support hate-speech detection in another language with comparable performance? To answer this question, we conduct a large-scale study across 14 languages. \change{We observe consistent patterns in which certain language pairs transfer more effectively than others. Among the factors we measure, linguistic similarity is the strongest predictor of these patterns, with temporal overlap and dataset-size difference playing smaller roles. These measurable factors do not fully explain the observed patterns; a complementary qualitative analysis suggests that shared cultural cues and communicative norms may be associated with some of the remaining cases, particularly within several clusters. We present this cultural interpretation as a hypothesis from qualitative inspection rather than a measured cause.}{} Our analysis includes low-resource languages, offering practical insights into when cross-lingual transfer can support them and where its limitations emerge. These findings inform the design of more reliable multilingual hate-detection systems.

papers.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
papers.abstract: As model parameters scale up, sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have become essential for model scaling. However, mainstream models currently adopt hierarchical architectures, where experts in different layers, although topologically independent, exhibit substantial similarity and redundancy in their stored content. Compared to the hierarchically arranged \textbf{Local Expert} in existing mainstream models, we hypothesize that inter-layer shared \textbf{Meta Expert} hold greater potential. To this end, we conduct a multi-dimensional empirical comparison between Local and Meta Experts, and find that models incorporating Meta Experts exhibit lower parameter redundancy, together with lower cross-entropy loss and higher downstream task accuracy. With the activated quantity and the expert granularity held fixed, \textbf{our model matches the performance of Vanilla MoE using only 70--80\% of the experts}, substantially improving the model's scaling potential. Beyond removing inter-layer redundancy among experts and improving information storage efficiency, our theoretical analysis further shows that, compared with Local Experts, Meta Experts provide hidden states with more flexible residual pathways, thereby improving information retrieval efficiency.

authors.name: Yicheng Gu
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures
papers.abstract: With Q-day approaching, the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) has begun, with governments across the US, UK and EU mandating migration to quantum-resistant standards. This paper benchmarks the three NIST-standardised PQC algorithms - FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) - across key generation, signing and verification operations, measuring both computational performance and energy consumption on a range of constrained IoT-class devices, from the 32-bit Raspberry Pi 1 and Zero to the 64-bit Raspberry Pi 4, as well as commodity laptop hardware. Using the FNIRSI FNB58 USB power meter and OpenSSL~3.5, results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA achieve energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography across all tested architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing is inadvisable on constrained hardware: energy costs for SLH-DSA signing on 32-bit devices were up to 243\% higher than on equivalent 64-bit hardware, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments. These findings have direct implications for IoT security practitioners planning PQC migration.

papers.title: Testing TLS 1.3 PQC on constrained devices and microcontrollers
papers.abstract: The UK, EU and US governments have set timelines for post-quantum cryptography migration of critical systems, with deadlines ranging from 2028 to 2035. This paper focuses on IoT-class devices and microcontrollers and the viability of using PQC to connect these devices in secure TLS 1.3 connections. Using wolfSSL, we benchmark a 36-combination TLS 1.3 algorithm matrix, pairing ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and X25519/ECC P-256 key exchange with ML-DSA-44/65/87, Ed25519, ECDSA, and RSA-PSS authentication, across four devices (Raspberry Pi Pico W & Pico 2 W, ESP32, and a Raspberry Pi Zero), measuring both handshake latency and energy consumption. We found that in capable devices, all choices in the TLS matrix gave similar results, but that in IoT-class devices, PQC performance is highly implementation- and architecture-dependent: the common assumption that elliptic-curve key exchange must be cheaper than post-quantum lattice-based key exchange does not hold in this wolfSSL-based implementation, where the best full-PQC combination (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) completes TLS handshakes 41% faster than the equivalent classical-modern pairing (X25519 + RSA-PSS) on the Pico W (up to 2.12x as energy-efficient, depending on the paired authentication algorithm), and 8.9x faster on the ESP32. Full-PQC, ML-KEM-512/ML-DSA-44, is not only possible but energy-competitive with or superior to Hybrid or Elliptic Curve alternatives on the most constrained devices, though ML-DSA's variable signing time means applications with strict latency-predictability budgets must accept this variance as the cost of full quantum-safe authentication. We further show that the IETF's draft-specified X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid incurs approximately the combined cost of its two components, rather than offering a performance compromise, making pure ML-KEM the more practical choice on hardware lacking Curve25519 assembly support.

papers.title: Ionized Gas Kinematics and Star-forming Clumps in Extremely Metal-poor Galaxies
papers.abstract: Extremely Metal Poor (XMP) galaxies are the least chemically evolved objects in the local Universe and provide important constraints on galaxy formation in low-metallicity environments. This work investigates the ionised gas kinematics and star formation properties of XMP galaxies to identify disturbed or multi-component gas motions and explore their connection with star formation. We analyse long-slit spectroscopic observations of nine XMP galaxies obtained with the Intermediate Dispersion Spectrograph on the 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope. The study uses the H$α$ emission line to trace ionised gas and emission-line ratios to derive gas-phase metallicities. The kinematic analysis reveals that some galaxies exhibit ordered rotation, with kinematic centres not always coincident with the luminous star-forming heads. Most systems show disturbed, asymmetric, or declining velocity profiles, while localized distortions near bright star-forming heads suggest that massive clumps influence the surrounding gas dynamics. We derive dynamical masses for the dominant clumps and investigate the mass--metallicity and size--metallicity relations. The clumps exhibit low metallicities consistent with the XMP regime and comparable to those observed in low-mass dwarf galaxies. Three galaxies show counter-rotating or kinematically decoupled ionised-gas components, indicating complex gas kinematics and possible external gas acquisition. Our sample is predominantly composed of isolated systems, with metal-poor star formation concentrated in compact head regions. These properties may reflect gas accretion through mergers, interactions, or the acquisition of metal-poor gas from the intergalactic medium and cosmic filaments. Internal processes such as outflows, gas mixing, recycling, and stochastic star formation may also contribute to the observed properties.

authors.name: Alejandro Lumbreras-Calle
authors.institution: Centro de Estudios de Física del Cosmos de Aragón

authors.name: Bruce G. Elmegreen
authors.institution: IBM Research - Thomas J. Watson Research Center

papers.title: Polyscene: Scenario Planning as Diversity Planning
papers.abstract: Scenario planning is a foresight practice in which analysts construct a small set of plausible futures and prepare an organisation for each. Each scenario is a narrative that must be plausible, internally consistent, relevant and challenging, and the set as a whole must be differentiated. The practice remains manual: a workshop (i.e., a facilitated meeting in which a small group of experts writes the narratives) considers only the factors it has time for, carries the biases of the experts who run it, and cannot be redone whenever conditions change. In this paper, we automate scenario planning by casting it as a diversity planning problem, in which two scenarios differ when they end in different narratives on the analyst's drivers. The result is a set of scenarios, one for each narrative that the topic can reach within a budget. Our implementation, Polyscene, is a generic engine that generates scenarios from a topic. We use geopolitical conflicts and shipping-route disruptions as case studies. For the first, we build the planning problem's initial state from the GDELT Project so it reflects current relationships among the countries involved. Polyscene then generates scenarios showing how relationships among those countries change. With a board of six countries as of 1 January 2021 and a budget of five events, the conflict set puts five of the 15 country pairs at war, and each of the three wars that break out among these countries by 1 January 2026 ends a scenario. For the second, we build the initial state from ship traffic, a supply-pressure index, and the news, and Polyscene generates scenarios showing what a closed or diverted route could do to a manufacturer's parts stock. With four routes per board and the same date and budget, each set includes three outcomes, and the Suez Canal set includes the March 2021 blockage and the December 2023 Red Sea container diversion.

papers.title: Beyond static torques: Self-consistent migration and dynamical trapping of low-mass planets in dusty disks
papers.abstract: The rapid inward migration of low-mass planets remains a primary theoretical challenge in planet formation. While recent studies show that the solid component of protoplanetary disks can exert strong positive torques to counteract the negative gas torques, traditional static fixed-orbit models fail to capture the fully coupled dynamics of a migrating planet. In this work, we present 2D high-resolution, two-fluid hydrodynamical simulations using a comoving reference frame to track the self-consistent orbital evolution of embedded planets across a comprehensive six-dimensional parameter space. By allowing the planet to dynamically respond to disk-exerted torques, we identify a wide diversity of migration regimes, involving inward/outward migration and oscillatory radial confinement. We also find that massive cores can overcome dust-induced barriers, experiencing dust-mediated runaway outward or inward migration. Conversely, in dust-rich environments continuous gas-dust momentum exchange combined with planet torques dynamically regenerates co-orbital dust asymmetries, creating robust dynamical attractors where super-Earths undergo stable, oscillatory confinement, effectively halting inward drift without requiring pre-existing pressure bumps or disk substructures. This self-induced trapping mechanism could be relevant in the outer disk, beyond the water-ice line in environments with a enhanced local dust-to-gas ratio, where icy pebbles are moderately coupled to the gas. In low-metallicity or highly diffusive disks, planets generally adopt monotonic inward decay, apart from cases with outward migration. Ultimately, the diversity of these self-consistent trajectories demonstrates that static torque approximations are insufficient. Evaluating fully coupled kinematic feedback is essential for accurately predicting planetary survival and the final architecture of planetary systems.

papers.title: Wielandt subgroups of nilpotent residuals and Fitting-height bounds
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, let $\mathrm W(G)$ be the intersection of the normalizers of the nilpotent residuals of the subnormal subgroups of $G$, and let $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ be the length of the associated upper series. Thus $\mathrm W(G)=G$ exactly when all these residuals are normal in $G$. We prove that every finite soluble group satisfies $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)\le h(G)\le4\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Fitting height, and that $h(G)\le3\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ if $|G|$ is odd or the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $G$ are abelian. Both constants are attained at every length, the constant $4$ by $\{2,3\}$-groups. Moreover, every pair $(n,h)$ with $n\le h\le4n$ occurs as $(\ell_{\mathrm W}(G),h(G))$. The constant $4$ comes from primitive groups. A soluble primitive group $V\rtimes M$ satisfies $\mathrm W(V\rtimes M)=V\rtimes M$ if and only if every abelian subgroup of $\mathrm F(M)$ is cyclic. It then has Fitting height four if and only if $\mathrm F(M)=C\times Q_8$, with $C$ cyclic, and $M$ induces the full group $\mathrm{Out}(Q_8)\cong S_3$. We also determine when the base group of a soluble regular wreath product is the first term of the series.

papers.title: Elements of the Green ring related to Alperin's weight conjecture
papers.abstract: J. L. Alperin introduced his celebrated weight conjecture, a major question in the modular representation theory of finite groups, which has now been studied for several decades. Alperin viewed this conjecture as the beginning of a ``Lie theory for the general finite group", as the title of the article indicates. This paper is intended as a tribute to Alperin's insight. In this note, we place an emphasis on projective modules and putting the numerical questions arising from the weight conjecture into a ``module form" within the appropriate Green ring of RG, when G is a finite group, and R is a suitable complete discrete valuation ring with residue field of prime characteristic p. We believe that this work moves in the direction of a structural approach to Alperin's weight conjecture.

papers.title: MIMOS-Tools: An Integrated Toolchain for Model-Based Design of Embedded Systems
papers.abstract: Despite decades of progress in model-based methods and tools for embedded real-time systems, there is still no integrated environment that supports the entire development lifecycle. This paper presents MIMOS-Tools, a comprehensive toolchain spanning the key phases of development, including modeling, simulation, formal verification, real-time scheduling, schedulability and end-to-end latency analysis, and code generation for heterogeneous multicore platforms. All phases are grounded in a single, coherent, and deterministic model of computation, the MIMOS model, for which we present a formal operational semantics and establish both functional and timing determinism. This semantic foundation ensures that properties verified at the model level are preserved throughout the development process and in the generated implementation. A distinguishing feature of MIMOS-Tools is its support for not only deterministic but also modular, compositional design. Unlike synchronous design environments such as SCADE and Simulink, which rely on a global base clock and offline static scheduling, MIMOS-Tools supports time-triggered asynchronous communication together with flexible real-time scheduling of computation. This removes the tight global coupling of the synchronous paradigm: components can be added, modified, or updated without recomputing a system-wide schedule, enabling scalable and incremental design and dynamic updates throughout the system lifecycle. However, MIMOS-Tools also supports Simulink models when the deadlines of tasks are set to zero to emulate the zero-time semantics of synchronous design. The toolchain is available at uu-mimos.github.io.

papers.title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
papers.abstract: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $ρ(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $ρ(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Blažej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $ρ(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $Θ(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.

authors.name: Fatemeh Emami
authors.institution: Shahid Sadoughi University of Medical Sciences and Health Services

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

papers.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not available during the forecasting phase. In this article, we address this challenge. We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting. We evaluate these approaches on the ETT-small datasets, a standard benchmark for time-series forecasting, under both spike-based and continuous activation functions. We compare the proposed closed-loop approaches against state-of-the-art methods such as SpaceTime, as well as the zero-masking baseline in S4. Both of the proposed approaches perform comparably to or better than zero-masking with S4, and in most cases match SpaceTime. These findings highlight the trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized activations, and demonstrate that the proposed Deep SSM architectures provide a competitive framework for forecasting.

papers.title: Looks Fine to Me: Understanding Oversight in Agentic Interactions
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems are deployed to execute complex tasks across domains such as writing, coding, and data analysis. As execution is offloaded to AI agents, the human role shifts toward oversight. Effective oversight requires recognizing when closer scrutiny is needed, even though flawed outputs may appear convincing. Our formative study (N=12) revealed that users accepted plausible outputs without thorough evaluation, and only recognized these lapses in retrospect. To examine this systematically, we conducted a controlled within-subject study (N=36) in which participants completed programming tasks with an agent that produced correct outputs, silent defects, or visible failures. Combining task outcomes, interaction logs, gaze, physiological signals, and self-reports, we examined perceived, behavioral, and effective oversight. Participants were often highly confident while missing silent defects: they performed generic checks, failed to generate diagnostic evidence, or even misinterpreted defect evidence. We discuss how studying oversight across multiple dimensions can support future work on timely, task-calibrated re-engagement.

papers.title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
papers.abstract: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.

authors.name: Lutian Zhao
authors.institution: China Automotive Technology and Research Center

papers.title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $85$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.

papers.title: Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking
papers.abstract: A feed ranker scores candidates with a value model, a weighted sum of engagement predictions. Each prediction conflates a baseline, what this viewer, item or request would produce anyway, with the incremental amount by which this candidate exceeds it. The literature mostly removes the baseline. We argue that a multi-signal value model should keep the raw prediction and add the incremental part as a separately weighted term. On Instagram Feed, three debiasing families deployed independently, for viewer habit, item popularity and request context, are one parameterised operator, and a design procedure picks a point in it. Media-type (format) bias goes instead to a debiased label chosen by the same procedure. In a controlled four-arm ablation of deployed Feed terms (neither term, each alone, both), the two-term arm beats both single-term arms at production weights on point estimates in 11 of 13 judged (term, metric) pairs. Of the 26 direct contrasts, 17 are significantly for it and only 1 against it, on impressions. The ablation also suggests that the offline diagnostic should screen signals, not rank them. Such terms have served Instagram Feed production for most of a year. Beyond Feed, Meta, whose apps serve billions of people, has adopted the operator across surfaces, apps and both ranking stages. Its launches there drive sessions and daily active users, the core visitation and retention metrics.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Distributed Radio Map Estimation in Decentralized Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning based radio map estimation (RME) approaches rely on frequent exchange of high-dimensional model updates and often require a central server for collaboration coordination and update aggregation. This incurs prohibitively high communication overhead, rendering them impractical for bandwidth-constrained mobile and wireless edge networks. Moreover, in practical mobile sensing scenarios, sparse and unevenly collected measurements lead to estimation uncertainty, which is critical for guiding RME and collaboration among distributed nodes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an uncertainty-aware distributed radio map estimation (UA-D-RME) framework for decentralized networks. In UA-D-RME, each node locally infers a probabilistic model from its sparse measurements to estimate both its local radio map and the associated estimation uncertainty. Instead of exchanging raw data or model updates, neighboring nodes communicate only low-dimensional statistical information, including radio map and uncertainty measures over their overlapping monitoring areas. An uncertainty-aware statistical consensus mechanism is then developed to iteratively align probabilistic models in neighborhood by ensuring consistency on estimation confidence. Theoretical analysis establishes the convergence of the proposed consensus mechanism and characterizes the distributed generalization performance of the proposed UA-D-RME method. Experiments on urban radio map datasets verify that UA-D-RME achieves desired reconstruction accuracy comparable to the centralized RME benchmark while reducing communication costs and without exchanging raw measurements.

authors.name: Songyang Zhang
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Finite-Size CV-QKD for Satellite Quantum Communication under a Hybrid Noise Model
papers.abstract: Satellite-based continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is fundamentally constrained by finite communication windows, channel attenuation, and statistical fluctuations arising from a limited number of exchanged quantum states. This work develops a finite-size CV-QKD framework for satellite quantum communication under a hybrid noise model that jointly incorporates satellite geometry, atmospheric and propagation losses, quantum Poissonian noise coexisting with classical additive white Gaussian noise, detector imperfections, and composable finite-key security under collective attacks. A single canonical finite-size secret key rate (SKR) expression is derived in which the finite-size correction is stated in a strictly decreasing form in the block size, removing the ambiguity between the segmented and the block-level formulations used in earlier treatments. The finite-size accounting is further extended to the quantum bit error ratio (QBER) through an explicit parameter estimation penalty, so that the feasibility constraint inherits the same block-size dependence as the key rate. The framework quantifies the influence of reconciliation efficiency, transmission efficiency, detection efficiency, receiver aperture, beam waist, zenith angle, wavelength, and effective communication time. Numerical results reveal a significant performance gap between finite-size and asymptotic operation, indicating that asymptotic analysis can overestimate the feasible satellite altitude by a factor of several, and that the achievable range is governed by the number of signals actually exchanged rather than by any single physical channel parameter. These results establish block size as a first-class design variable for satellite CV-QKD mission dimensioning.

papers.title: On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of Östergård--Paavola and Ó Catháin--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.

papers.title: Translation and data ethics
papers.abstract: This chapter introduces data ethics for translation and discusses a number of ethical issues regarding data. These include issues of copyright, ownership and bias, which apply to all types of data, whereas there are further issues particular to minoritised language communities and those on either side of the digital divide, as data is implicated in power imbalances and dynamics. We close with a discussion of responsibility and regulation, and reflect on the growing attention on data ethics from translation studies researchers.

papers.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
papers.abstract: Despite substantial progress in Deep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce the OpenDS task, designed to evaluate agents' ability to perform multi-step deep search in the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect relevant evidence from multiple independent sources through Web search, browser interaction, and evidence processing, and ultimately determine a unique factual answer. Building on this task formulation, we construct OpenDS-World, a benchmark comprising 200 challenging tasks spanning diverse information modalities, heterogeneous file formats, and interactive access requirements, with independent human verification to ensure evidence validity and answer uniqueness. We evaluate 12 frontier models under a unified tool environment and execution protocol. The best-performing model achieves 39.0% accuracy, while human evaluation across 1,000 independent attempts yields 21.1% accuracy. Further analyses of tool usage, search cost, termination behavior, and failure recovery reveal substantial differences in research strategies across models, as well as persistent challenges in tool coordination and long-horizon search management. OpenDS-World provides a unified evaluation platform for systematically assessing and advancing agents' autonomous deep search capabilities in real-world open Web environments.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter
papers.abstract: Emoji are widely treated as compact affective tokens whose meaning is summarised by a single sentiment score. We argue that this picture is incomplete. From a corpus of 16{,}575 English tweets and a per-emoji metric we call \emph{stability delta} (within-class minus between-class cosine similarity of sentence embeddings), we show that emojis used in tightly clustered topical contexts also exhibit \emph{more} polarised crowd-sourced sentiment, not less. Validated against the Kralj Novak et al.\ (2015) sentiment lexicon, the central correlation is Spearman $ρ= +0.361$ (Holm $p = 0.015$, 95\% bootstrap CI $[+0.10, +0.59]$); against the independent Ferré et al.\ (2025) Spanish 13-emotion ratings, $ρ= +0.509$ ($p = 0.0003$). The result survives permutation testing, BCa bootstrap, leave-one-out jackknife, partial correlation controlling for emoji frequency, and Holm correction across a four-test family. Topical coherence and affective dispersion are distinct dimensions of emoji meaning. As a downstream check we report leakage-free five-fold cross-validation results for sarcasm classification on the Emoji Sarcasm Dataset; all three baselines (a gated multimodal architecture, fine-tuned BERTweet features, and fine-tuned RoBERTa features) score above 0.97 macro F1, indicating the dataset has saturating emoji-label cues. We frame the classifier as supporting evidence rather than the contribution.

papers.title: Exact Envy-Free Cake Cutting with Polynomial Expected Queries
papers.abstract: Envy-free cake cutting asks how to divide a resource so that no agent prefers another agent's share. Finding such a division with few queries about preferences has been a longstanding challenge. Aziz and Mackenzie gave the first query bound depending only on the number $n$ of agents: a tower of six $n$'s. Subsequent improvements culminated in Ye and Bai's single-exponential bound of $n^{O(1)}2^n$. A large gap remains between this deterministic upper bound and Procaccia's general lower bound of $Ω(n^2)$. Whether polynomially many queries suffice is a central open question in fair division. We show that a polynomial expected query bound is possible. Our randomised protocol uses only independent, uniformly sampled points from the cake as its source of randomness. For every profile of $n$ agents with nonnegative, additive, nonatomic valuations, the protocol has the following guarantees: (1) It terminates with probability one. (2) Every allocation it returns is complete and exactly envy-free. (3) Its expected number of Robertson-Webb queries is $\widetilde{O}(n^{30})$. The expectation is taken solely over the protocol's random choices, with no distributional assumptions on preferences.

papers.title: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we propose SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases. Then, we evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and find that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks. For example, GPT-5.6-Sol as a supervisor suffers an ASR of up to 0.93. Mitigation strategies such as prompting and restricted communication fail to reduce the risk consistently. These results show that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.

papers.title: From Partitioning to Provisioning: Co-Designing DNN Deployment and Infrastructure Capacity
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) partitioning enables distributed inference by dividing model computation across interconnected devices. Existing approaches have largely focused on optimizing DNN deployment over infrastructure with fixed computing and communication capacities. Yet when these resources cannot adequately support inference demands, optimizing deployment alone is insufficient: the supporting infrastructure must also be provisioned. Crucially, deployment and provisioning are inherently coupled. How a DNN is partitioned determines where capacity is needed, while capacity provisioning can fundamentally change the preferred deployment. Motivated by this interdependence, we investigate the co-design of DNN deployment and infrastructure capacity for pipelined inference. Despite the coupling between these decisions, we reveal an efficiently solvable structure: on acyclic networks, the problem admits an exact shortest-path reformulation, enabling globally optimal joint design in polynomial time. Numerical evaluations demonstrate the benefits of co-design over treating deployment and provisioning separately, highlighting the potential of inference-driven infrastructure planning.

authors.name: Zongyao Huang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
papers.abstract: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus, feed the encoder a raw amplitude view and an instance-normalized shape view of the input through two small stems, and distill one specialist encoder per view into a single encoder. The result, TS2Vec-FM, is a 1.6M-parameter dilated convolutional network that, kept frozen, reaches 83.3% on UCR-128 and 75.3% on UEA-27 under linear probing, within 0.3 pp of MantisV2, the current state of the art, and above TS2Vec trained separately on each target dataset. What we find most interesting is how different TS2Vec-FM is from other foundation models in design: near-parity is reached without attention, without a patch tokenizer, and without intermediate-layer extraction, using an "old-school" convolutional encoder and a two-layer MLP stem.

papers.title: Tetrads and their intrinsic spin structures
papers.abstract: In Minkowski spacetime an observer's moving frame may be associated with a tetrad: four orthogonal directions, one timelike and three spacelike. Locally, a physical measurement is always made in relation to some tetrad, and relativistic spin measurements in particular raise subtleties because spin and momentum cannot be cleanly separated under Lorentz boosts. This paper shows that every tetrad is endowed with an intrinsic spin structure. Each spatial direction may be generated from the timelike direction by a linear operator, and the requirement that these generate an orthogonal tetrad for every timelike direction is sufficient, on its own, to endow them with the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the Pauli algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{3,0}(\mathbb{R})$ and the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ simultaneously. These generators serve three roles at once: they build the spatial legs of every tetrad, they generate the Lorentz boosts between tetrads, and they endow each tetrad with an intrinsic spin structure. The eigenvectors of the spin generators form a null-ray tetrad which is simultaneously a Newman--Penrose-type frame and the set of Dirac rest spinors, while the invertibility of boosts between tetrads yields the Dirac factorisation of the mass-shell condition. Minimal coupling of gauge and spinor fields is forced rather than imposed, the potential being absorbed by the covariant derivative because the path dependence of the phase prevents it from being incorporated by the spinor phase. Wigner rotations, relativistic spin correlations, quantum reference frames and the Coulomb problem are examined within this tetrad framework. This framework is equivalent to the Hilbert-space formalism of relativistic quantum mechanics wherever the two have been compared, and so offers a geometric formulation of that formalism rather than an alternative to it.

papers.title: SHAM-Bench: A Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks
papers.abstract: Span-level hallucination detection pinpoints unsupported content in LLM outputs, enabling actionable feedback and targeted mitigation. Existing evaluations for span-level hallucination detection methods are fragmented across tasks, annotation formats, and metrics, and most span-level datasets cover only a single NLG domain, making it difficult to assess whether a detection method actually generalizes across tasks and domains. In this paper, we introduce SHAM-Bench (Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks), a unified benchmark for span-level hallucination detection spanning six NLG tasks, aggregated from existing human-annotated datasets totaling 6,461 examples under a common schema and evaluation protocol. Using SHAM-Bench, we evaluate existing hallucination detection methods and find that fine-tuned detectors often perform well in-domain but degrade under distribution shift, whereas prompt-based methods with reasoning are more robust across tasks. Our analysis further shows that subtle unsupported content remains difficult to detect and span-level evaluation is still challenged by ambiguous span boundaries and noisy labels. We release the dataset, evaluation code, and a public leaderboard to support future research on broadly generalizable hallucination detection.

papers.title: GALA: Geometry-Aware Language Model for Controllable Object Arrangement
papers.abstract: Reasoning about fine-grained placement constraints, such as support and containment, is essential for realistic 3D scene creation. It remains a significant challenge for existing methods that rely on simplified object representations like oriented bounding box (OBB), which are blind to the detailed geometry. To address this limitation, we introduce GALA, a geometry-aware language model with explicit point cloud perception for controllable object placement. Our model performs autoregressively by predicting the 6D pose of one target object at a time conditioned on the scene context and placement instruction. We utilize a two-stage training strategy: the first stage aligns geometric and textual modalities through pretraining tasks, and the second stage fine-tunes the model for placement. To facilitate this task, we also curate a multi-source scene dataset covering diverse room types and fine-grained furniture arrangements, which will be open-sourced for community benefit. Experiments on our benchmark show our model significantly outperforms baselines without explicit geometric reasoning. We further develop a multi-stage plan-place-verify agent pipeline that uses the model for text-driven scene generation. Project Page: https://xccelephant.github.io/paper/gala/

papers.title: SITO: Sifting a Commercial Text-Safety API for Missed Harm and False Flags in English, Ukrainian and Surzhyk
papers.abstract: Platforms that host young users screen messages with commercial text-safety APIs, but independent evidence on how often such systems miss harm or flag harmless text is scarce, especially outside English, and the documentation of the one studied here leaves its false-positive rate unquantified. We evaluated one such API, Tuteliq Detect as deployed under the release identifier tuteliq-detect-v5.20261011 (not the separately published v6 model), on six harm categories: authorised push-payment fraud, money-mule recruitment, social engineering, romance scams, gambling harm and bullying. We built SITO (Synthetic Independent Text-safety benchmark with Overflagging tests; sito is Ukrainian for 'sieve'), 2,332 synthetic cases in English, Ukrainian and mixed Ukrainian, with each harmful case matched by hard harmless ones: same-topic messages, minimal-edit contrasts, warnings and retrospective accounts. On English text the system flagged 84.9-94.1% of harmful cases and 0-4.3% of harmless ones per category. It missed third-party reports of ongoing harm far more often than perpetrators' messages (63.6% against 95.1% recall, all languages), when sent without the settings the API offers for reports of harm. Ukrainian and mixed-language input was detected at least as often as English, recall was lower on text from a held-out generator family, so headline recall may be optimistic, and 3.2% of cases received a different decision in repeated runs. A platform should measure false positives on its own traffic and check how bystander reports are handled. The datasets, generation prompts and code are released.

authors.name: Andrii Tuzhykov
authors.institution: State institution "South Ukrainian National Pedagogical University named after K. D. Ushynsky"

papers.title: Evaluating Runtime Prediction and Conservative Walltime Policies in HPC Systems
papers.abstract: Efficient use of large-scale supercomputing systems depends on accurate runtime estimation and walltime selection. To avoid premature termination, users often overestimate walltime, leading to poor resource utilization and reduced scheduling efficiency. This paper presents a predictor-agnostic framework for safe walltime recommendation in production HPC environments. Rather than proposing a new runtime prediction model, the primary contribution is the SAFE decision layer, which converts predicted runtimes into conservative bounded walltime recommendations suitable for deployment. Runtime prediction is therefore treated as a modular component within the proposed framework. We evaluate the approach using large-scale production job histories from the Fugaku and NREL Eagle supercomputers, comprising approximately 24M and 11M jobs, respectively. Runtime prediction performance is first evaluated using representative predictors, including linear regression, neural networks, and a neural ensemble. The proposed SAFE framework is then evaluated using the NN ensemble predictor. Experimental results indicate that similarity-aware prediction substantially improves runtime estimation for workloads similar to previous executions. When combined with the proposed conservative walltime recommendation policies, these improvements enable walltime gap reductions of approximately 20 - 26% while maintaining job termination rates below 1% across both systems.

papers.title: A mean value formula for the p-Laplacian
papers.abstract:
In this paper we introduce an asymptotic mean value formula of the form $u(x) - \B_ε^p (u) (x) =ε^2 Δ_p u(x) + o(ε^2)$ for the $p-$Laplacian, $\plap u := 
abla \cdot  ig( |
abla u |^{p-2} 
abla u  ig)$. Here $\B_ε^p (u)$ is a nonlinear expression that involve the mean value and the surmemum/infimum of $u$ in suitable balls. This asymptotic mean value formula allows us to characterize viscosity solutions to equations with different homogeneities in different sets of variables, like $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=f(x)$ (for $x=(x',x'') \in\mathbb{R}^d$, $x'=(x_1,...,x_n)$ and $x''=(x_{n+1,...,x_d})$), and the parabolic $p$-Laplace heat equation $\partial_t u (x,t)-Δ_p u(x,t)=0$. Moreover, the resulting asymptotic mean value formulas are related to two-player zero sum games whose value functions, characterized as the unique solution to the corresponding dynamic programming principle, converge as the parameter that controls the size of the steps in the game goes to zero, to the unique viscosity solution to the corresponding boundary value problem for the operator under consideration. Finally, we also include a Holder regularity result for $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=0$ proved using the game theoretical interpretation of the problem.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Estimation and Inference for Longitudinal Win Probabilities with Ordinal Outcomes in Observational Studies
papers.abstract: Repeated ordinal outcomes capture how treatment benefits and harms evolve over time. We develop doubly robust estimation and inference for visit-specific win probabilities and their prespecified weighted summaries, with Desirability of Outcome Ranking as a motivating example. Baseline confounding is addressed through augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) of treatment-specific marginal category probabilities or joint multinomial targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). We consider fold-specific and pooled targeting and establish conditions for double-robust consistency and semiparametric efficiency under participant-level cross-fitting. When only one nuisance model is correctly specified, inference based only on the efficient influence function may be invalid. For smooth parametric nuisance models, we derive covariance corrections from the complete estimating procedure, including targeting. When a correctly specified propensity model is estimated by maximum likelihood, a simplified score correction accommodates convergent flexible outcome learners without requiring their derivatives. The corrected covariance estimators retain within-participant dependence and support visit-specific, weighted-summary, and joint inference across repeated assessments. Simulations supported double robustness, demonstrated the importance of cross-fitting with overfit learners, and showed improved marginal and joint confidence coverage with the proposed corrections. TMLE, particularly with pooled targeting, often had lower root mean squared error under adequate treatment overlap, whereas AIPW was more stable under weak overlap. An electronic health record study of hospitalized adults with an acute respiratory illness illustrates how the trajectory and weighted summary reveal complementary aspects of the treatment comparison.

papers.title: CAPS: Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis for Missing MRI Imputation in Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.abstract: Multi-parametric MRI is the gold standard for neuro-oncology, yet acquiring complete 4-modality protocols may be unfeasible in real-world clinical practice. When handling missing modalities, existing automated systems force a critical compromise: robust segmenters operate as uninterpretable "black boxes" that bypass image generation, while standard synthesis models often produce blurry reconstructions lacking diagnostic reliability. To address this issue, we propose CAPS, a Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis framework that reconciles computational precision with clinical transparency. Our multi-modal generative architecture is driven by a hybrid objective function (L_1 + L_AFP + L_DualDice) that explicitly enforces the preservation of deep anatomical features and strict topological boundaries, rather than relying solely on pixel-wise optimization. Evaluated comprehensively on the BraTS Adult Glioma dataset, the framework achieves superior synthesis fidelity across intensity-based metrics, and demonstrates robust downstream segmentation performance (82.38% mean Dice), successfully restoring verifiable visual context. Furthermore, the framework exhibits exceptional zero-shot cross-domain generalization, maintaining high structural fidelity across completely unseen Meningioma, Pediatric, and Sub-Saharan African cohorts without domain-specific adaptation. Finally, a blinded radiological assessment confirms that our anatomy-aware approach significantly enhances both perceived image quality and clinical utility, providing clinicians with the reliable visual evidence required to trust downstream automated workflows.

authors.name: Arthur Longuefosse
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Integrative Medical Sciences

papers.title: What Not to Erase: Saliency-Constrained Augmentation for Low-Resource Handwritten Character Recognition
papers.abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and handwritten character recognition (HCR) in low-resource historical material collections often rely on data augmentation, yet augmentation strategies are typically evaluated almost exclusively through predictive accuracy. This leaves open whether a model's improved performance is accompanied by saliency stability. This question is important in low-resource historical HCR, where recognition is performed on variable and partially degraded letterforms and two models with similar predictive performance may differ in how consistently their saliency patterns respond to such variation. We therefore study saliency-guided augmentation as an explanation-aware strategy for low-resource HCR. Rather than treating saliency maps only as post-hoc interpretations, we use them to define augmentation variants that perturb, preserve, or constrain visually informative regions of character images. We compare classical document-style transformations, random lacunae, and several saliency-constrained lacuna variants. To evaluate the effect of augmentation beyond accuracy, we introduce the Explainability Consistency Index (ECI), a metric that quantifies the stability of saliency patterns under controlled perturbations. We find that saliency-constrained augmentation can improve recognition over classical augmentation, but no single saliency strategy is consistently best. The preferred form of the constraint varies with both architecture and corpus, indicating that saliency is better treated as a mechanism for controlling augmentation than as a fixed augmentation strategy. In some settings, saliency-constrained training improves explanation consistency even when predictive performance is similar. This shows that predictive metrics alone can obscure differences in model sensitivity under perturbation, motivating explanation consistency as a complementary evaluation dimension.

papers.title: NousDB - A Fast Query Engine for Semantic Analytics
papers.abstract: Semantic data analytics systems integrate AI-powered operators into query pipelines, enabling declarative queries over structured and unstructured data. However, existing systems rely on per-tuple model invocations, ad hoc operator designs, and lack principled cost models, resulting in poor scalability and limited optimization. We present NousDB, a high-performance semantic analytics engine built on Apache DataFusion[22]. Through NousDB we propose an extended relational algebra with three semantic operators and formal algebraic properties that enable principled query rewriting and cross-operator optimization. We further propose a token-based cost model using equi-depth token histograms to optimize batch sizing under context-window constraints and provide statistical guarantees for safe batching. Experiments show that NousDB achieves up to x86 speedups with both local and enterprise LLMs, while leading competitors in token efficiency and accuracy. These gains extend to complex JOB and Stack workloads augmented with semantic operators, supporting both traditional and semantic analytics.
